ἐκβάλλω.definition: throw ashore, .. Od.19.278; .. .. Hdt.6.44; Id.7.170 :—Med., put ashore, Hdt.6.101; jettison, Syngr. ap. D.35.11

ἐκβάω.definition: Dor. for Foed. Dor. ap. Th.5.77

ἐκβλέπω.definition: look, Philostr.Jun.Im.I, cf; get the power of sight, Ael.NA3.25

ἐκβολβίζω.definition: peel, as one does an onion of its outer; metaph., uproot, destroy, Com.Adesp.992

ἐκβόλιον.definition: drug or other means for expelling the

ἔκβολος.definition: thrown out or away, exposed; frustrated, LXXJu.11.11

ἐκβυρσόω.definition: cause to project from the skin, Gal.18.721

ἐκβύρσωμα.definition: projecting of the bones out of the skin, ib.714

ἐκγελάω.definition: Ep. aor. h.Merc.389, Theoc.4.37; —laugh out, laugh loud, Od.16.354, 18.35, cf. X.Cyr.1.3.9, etc.; Pl.R.473c; Arist.Pr.965a24; metaph. of a liquid that rushes out with a gurgling sound, E.Tr.1176

ἐκγίγνομαι.definition: later and Ion. fut; c. dat., to be born to, .. Il.14.115, cf. Hdt.1.30,4.155; fut. perf., h.Ven.197

ἐκδέρω.definition: Ion. fut. strip off the skin; cudgel soundly, 'hide', Ar.V.450, Pl.R.616a, Hyp.Fr.200, PSI4.403 ; — Pass., Macho ap.Ath.13.580b

ἐκδέχομαι.definition: mostly of persons; take or receive from another, Il.13.710; A.Ch.762; of a beacon-fire, .. Id.Ag.285; take it on oneself, D.19.37

ἐκδέω.definition: bind so as to hang from, fasten to or on, c. gen., Od.10.96; they bound the oaks to the mules, i.e. they yoked the mules to them, Il.23.121; Aen.Tact.11.6; abs., bind planks behind, Od.22.174; E.Andr.556; metaph., tra…

ἐκδημέω.definition: to be abroad, to be on one's travels; c. acc., travel through, IG14.905

ἐκδημία.definition: going or being abroad, E.Fr.768: pl; metaph., departure from life, AP3.5

ἐκδίδωμι.definition: give out of one's house; give one's daughter in marriage, Hdt.1.196, E.IA132 , cf. Thphr.Char.22.4; having provided for their marriage at their own expense, D.27.69; D.S.4.53; freq. also without any acc., give in marr…

ἐκδιψάω.definition: to be parched with drought, of plants, Thphr.CP5.9.3; of a person, to be very thirsty, Plu.Cleom.29

ἔκδοτος.definition: given up, delivered, esp. betrayed; given in marriage, PMasp.5.10

ἐκδρομή.definition: running out, sally, charge, X.HG3.2.4; abstr. for concrete, party of skirmishers, Th.4.127

ἐκδύω.definition: causal in pres. impf. fut. aor. 1 late pf. AP5.72 :— take off, strip off, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, they stripped me of my cloak, Od.14.341; .. A.Ag.1269; X.Cyr.1.3.17; c. acc. only, strip, D.24.204; Id.54.8

ἔκζεσις.definition: boiling out or over, breaking out; = foreg., Erot. s.v

ἐκθάλλω.definition: put forth blossoms, Sm.Ca.2.13, Al.Hb.3.17; metaph., become active, of heat in the ground, Adam. ap. Aët.3.163

ἐκθεόω.definition: = , Ael.NA10.23, Porph.Marc.17; of temples or places, consecrate, App.BC3.3

ἐκθερίζω.definition: reap or mow completely, of a crop; cut out, Anacreont.9.7

ἔκθεσις.definition: exposure, of a child, Hdt.1.116; setting forth, exposition, Arist.APr.48a25, 49b6

ἔκθετος.definition: sent out of the house, sent away; projecting, salient, Sor.1.68; opp. Heliod.ap. Orib.49.4.23

ἐκθλίβω.definition: squeeze out, Arist.HA578b4, 626a20; Pass., to be crowded, cramped, of troops, X.An.3.4.19

ἐκθρῴσκω.definition: fut. aor. out of,c.gen., Il.16.427; 7.182, cf. 23.353; A.Pers.457; of the violent beating of the heart, 11.10.95; abs., leap forth, 21.539, cf. Corn.ND19; rarely c.acc., AP9.371; start up, Luc.DMar.2.3; come from the …

ἔκθυσις.definition: atonement, expiatory; averting by sacrifices, Iamb.Myst.9.3, cf.1.13

ἐκθώπτω.definition: aor. gain by flattery, wheedle over, S.Fr.857

ἐκκαθαίρω.definition: with acc. of the thing cleansed, clear out, Il.2.153; Hdt.l.c.; Hp.Mul.1.88, Orib.Syn.5.25.3; he clears this land of monsters, A.Supp.264; Luc.DDeor.13.1; clear him of all roughness, polish him up, metaph. from the fi…

ἐκκαλέω.definition: call out or forth, summon forth, Il.24.582; call forth, elicit, A.Ag.270; Aeschin.2.3; D.4.42, cf. Pl.Euthd.288d; Antiph.217.23; entice, provoke to battle, Plb.1.19.2, cf. Ascl.Tact.7.1

ἐκκαυλίζω.definition: pull out the stalk: metaph., pull off the sprouts, i.e. the profits, Ar.Eq.825

ἐκκείρω.definition: shear completely, shorn; cut off, A.R.4.1033

ἐκκενόω.definition: poet. empty out, leave desolate; unsheath, LXXEz.5.2

ἐκκηρύσσω.definition: Att. proclaim by voice of; cashier, 'drum out' of the army, prob. in Arist.Ath.61.2

ἐκκλέπτω.definition: aor. 2 Pass. X.HG5.4.12; —steal and; to deceive him, S.Ph.55, cf. 968; .. disguise not the matter, speak not falsely, Id.Tr.437

ἐκκλησία.definition: assembly duly summoned, less; = Lat. Comitia, = Comitia Centuriata, Curiata, D.H.4.20

ἔκκλισις.definition: turning out of one's course; tendency, Arist.Pr.863b24

ἔκκλυσμα.definition: that which is washed away, Plu.2.1089b; that which is washed up, produce of the sea, of purple dye, Zos.Alch.p.164 B. one must wash out, Aët.16.89

ἐκκναίω.definition: wear out: metaph. of troublesome loquacity, Theoc.15.88

ἐκκοπή.definition: cutting out, Phld.Ir.p.33 W; mutilation, Vett.Val.110.10

ἔκκριτος.definition: picked out, select, a chosen; evacuated, Arist.Pr.861a36

ἐκκυβεύω.definition: play at dice: metaph; Pass., to be gambled out of, lose at play, Plu.Art.17

ἐκκυέω.definition: bring forth, put forth as leaves, AP7.385

ἐκκυλίνδω.definition: roll out, Ar.Pax134; mostly; extricate, Pi.Fr.7, cf. AP7.176 :—Pass., to be extricated from, A.Pr.87; X.Cyn.8.8, cf. Plu.Galb.27

ἐκκυμαίνω.definition: swerve, bulge from the straight line, of a; cause to burst from their sockets, Herod.6.68

ἐκκύπτω.definition: peep out of, Babr.50.13; trans., put forth, Ael.NA15.21

ἐκλανθάνω.definition: escape notice utterly:—Med., forget utterly; causal in pres. with aor. 1 Aeol. : Ep. redupl. aor. 2

ἐκλεπτύνω.definition: make very thin, f.l. for Gp.16.6.3; reduce to a fine state, Syn.Alch.p.58B

ἐκλεπυρόω.definition: strip off the bark: metaph., strip, Sophr.22

ἐκλινάω.definition: escape out of the net, Eust.574.30

ἐκλογέω.definition: select, CPHerm.p.80; mostly in Med., excuse oneself, App.BC5.77; plead in excuse, ib.13: c. acc. et inf., to state by way of excuse that.., ib.3.48; Them.Or.8.103d

ἐκλύω.definition: v. set free, from labours; unloose, unstring a bow, Hdt.2.173; E.Hipp.825; likely to let loose a foolish tongue, S.Aj.1225

ἐκμυελίζω.definition: suck the marrow out of, deprive of strength, LXXNu.24.8

ἐκμυζάω.definition: suck out, Il.4.218, cf. Luc.Tim.8, Ael.NA3.39, Gal.UP6.15, Q.S.4.398; exhaust air from a vessel, HeroSpir. I Praef.: metaph., extort, Lyd.Mag.3.67; —also in form Dsc.Eup.1.62, Phlp.in Mete.115.18; —Pass., Antyll. ap. …

ἐκμυθόω.definition: make into a or fable, Philostr.Im.1.3

ἐκναρκάω.definition: become quite torpid or sluggish, Plu.Cor.31

ἐκνέμω.definition: pasture, Ph.2.233; —more freq. in Med; go forth to feed: metaph. in Med., S.Aj.369

ἐκνήφω.definition: fut. LXXGe.9.24; —sleep off a drunken fit; trans., carry off, LXXSi.34.2

ἐκξέω.definition: wipe off, erase, App. Anth.7.56,71, Tz.ad Lyc.874

ἔκπαγλος.definition: Ep. and Ion. word, terrible, violent; of persons, of Achilles, Il.21.589; also of Achilles, 1.146, 18.170; of other heroes, 20.389, 21.452

ἐκπαιφάσσω.definition: rush madly to the fray, Il.5.803

ἐκπαίω.definition: throw or cast out of a thing; intr., dash out, escape, Anaxil.22.17 :—Med., Plu.Brut.51

ἐκπαλαίω.definition: transgress the laws of wrestling, Philostr.Im.1.6

ἐκπατάσσω.definition: strike, afflict, E.HF890 : metaph., AP9.309 :—Pass., stricken in mind, Od.18.327; Hsch

ἐκπατέω.definition: withdraw from society, D.L.1.112; pf. part. having finished his walk, Id.4.19

ἐκπαύω.definition: strengthd. for set quite at rest, put an end to, E.Ion144 :—Med., take one's rest, Th.5.75

ἐκπέμπω.definition: bring out by calling, call or fetch out, Id.Ant.19:—so in Med., Id.OT951:—Pass., go forth, depart, Id.OC1664

ἐκπεράω.definition: abs., of an arrow, pass through, pierce, .. Il.13.652, cf. 16.346, etc.; of persons, go forth, X.Cyn.6.18; to Athens, Eub.10.5

ἐκπέρθω.definition: fut. destroy utterly, sack, of cities; take as booty from, Il.1.125

ἐκπέσσω.definition: Att. cook thoroughly: hence; of animals, digest or concoct food thoroughly, Hp.VM22

ἐκπέτασμα.definition: that which is spread out or; planisphere, Ptol.Geog.7.7 tit

ἐκπήδημα.definition: leap out, a height too great for over-leap, A.Ag.1376

ἐκπίεσμα.definition: that which is squeezed out; false form for , Gal.19.432, 14.782

ἐκπίνω.definition: fut. Amips.22.2; drain a cup dry, S.Fr.483; Pherecr.143.9; Antiph.3, etc.; also S.Ant.532

ἐκπίπτω.definition: of seafaring men, to be cast ashore, Od.7.283; Hdt.3.138; Id.8.13; E.Hel.1211; ib.539; Pl.Lg.866d; of things, suffer shipwreck, X.An.7.5.13; of fish, to be cast up, Arist.HA601b32

ἐκπλέω.definition: fut. pf. IG2.793a7; Ion; metaph., go out of one's mind, lose one's senses, Id.3.155, Ael.Fr.240

ἐκπνοή.definition: breathing out, exhalation, opp; death, J.AJ19.8.3

ἔκπνοος.definition: contr. breathless; breathing out, exhaling, Hp.Epid.6.6.1; smelling of.., Posidipp. ap.Ath.13.596c

ἐκποτάομαι.definition: Ion. = fly out or forth, of snowflakes, Il.19.357; of a ghost, Sapph.68.4: metaph., Theoc.11.72, 2.19

ἐκπτύσσω.definition: unfold, spread out, pf. part. Pass. prob. for Erot. s.v

ἐκπτύω.definition: fut. AP5.196 :—spit out; spit in token of disgust, Ar.V.792

ἐκπυρόω.definition: burn to ashes, consume utterly, E.IA1070; set on fire, Arist.Mete.341a18

ἐκπυρσεύω.definition: kindle, inflame: metaph., in Pass; give signals by a beacon-light, J.BJ4.10.5

ἐκραβδίζω.definition: flog out, drive out with a rod, Ar.Lys.576

ἐκρέω.definition: pf. : aor. Pass. in; of feathers, fall off, Ar.Av.104; of hair,Arist.HA518a32

ἐκρήγνυμι.definition: fut. S.Aj.775:—break off, snap; c. acc. cogn., let break forth, break out with, Plu.Fab.12; Luc.Cal.23:—Pass., break out, of an ulcer, Hdt.3.133; burst, of an abscess, Hp.Aph.4.82; .. A.Pr.369; of a quarrel, broke out…

ἔκρηξις.definition: breaking out, discharge; bursting asunder, Arist.Mu.395a15

ἐκσείω.definition: shake out or off; drive out or forth, Plu.Ant.14; reject it, D.S.18.66

ἐκσεύομαι.definition: Pass., pf. plpf. with sense of impf. , but usu. aor. : aor. I out or burst forth from, Il.7.1; Od.9.373; sleep fled away from his eyelids, 12.366: abs., rush out, Il.8.58; .. Od.9.438; the point burst out, Il.5.293 ; …

ἐκσηκόω.definition: weigh in the balance, assay, in Pass., Gloss

ἐκστρέφω.definition: turn inside out, Ar.Pl.721: metaph., change or alter entirely, Id.Nu.88; ib.554:—Pass., with feet turned outwards, Arist.Phgn.813a14; to be distorted, Gal.7.27

ἐκσῴζω.definition: Ep. :—preserve from danger, keep safe, Hdt.9.107, S.Aj.1128, etc.; E.El.28; to bring him safe.., Id.HF1222; Pl.Grg.486b:—Med., save oneself, Hdt.2.107; also, save for oneself, .. A.Pers.360; S.Ant.713:—Pass., .. when …

ἐκτανύω.definition: = Theoc.25.270:—Hom. has; extend, Epigr.Gr.1078.4 .— For S.OC1562, v. word, used by Hp.Fract.43. usu., but Anacreont.35.5 .]

ἐκτείνω.definition: fut. A.Pr.325, etc.:—stretch out; stretch, spread out a net, A.Ch.991; extend the line of an army, E.Heracl.801, Arr.Tact.5.6; E.Supp.654; X.HG6.5.19:—Pass., to be unfolded, smoothed, S.Fr.902

ἐκτελέω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.9.493, Od.4.7: Ep; of Time, Hes.Op.565, Hdt.6.69, Pi.P.4.104:—Pass., Od.11.294

ἐκτέμνω.definition: Ep. and Ion. , fut; cut trees out of a wood, cut down, Il.12.149, S.Tr.1196; also of planks, etc., hew out, hew into shape, Il.3.62, cf. 4.486; to cut the stumps out of the ground, Lys.7.19

ἐκτενής.definition: strained: hence of persons, warmly; extended, Dam.Pr.64; capable of extension, Herm.in Phdr.p.121A

ἐκτίθημι.definition: set up, offer for a prize, S.Fr.378; Plb.15.9.4; fix or grant allowances, rates of pay, etc., PSI5.498 , PEdgar2.4 , etc

ἐκτίνω.definition: Med., exact full payment for a thing, avenge, E.HF547; take vengeance on, Id.Med.267

ἐκτλάω.definition: bear, sustain to the end, aor.inf. Ph.2.464

ἔκτμημα.definition: section, segment, of the zones, Arist.Mete.362b5

ἐκτομάς.definition: wicket-gate, Aen.Tact.24.5; a kind of spear , Id

ἐκτομή.definition: cutting out, excision, Plu.Alc.16; castration, Hdt.3.48,49, Pl.Smp.195c , etc

ἔκτομον.definition: black hellebore, Hp.Mul.1.78; stone forming interior angle, Rev.Phil.29.240 , 49.6

ἐκτοξεύω.definition: shoot out, shoot away; metaph., reject, banish, Ph.1.528:—Pass., ib.252

ἐκτόπισις.definition: removal from a place, deportation, Gloss

ἔκτοπος.definition: away from a place, c. gen; foreign, strange, by no strange hand, S.Tr.1132

ἔκτρημα.definition: hole made in trepanning, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.16

ἔκτριμμα.definition: sore caused by rubbing; rubber, towel, Philox.2.41

ἐκτρόπιον.definition: everted eyelid, a disease in which the lid is turned outward, opp. Cels.7.7, Antyll. ap. Aët.7.74, Dem.Ophth.ib.73

ἔκτροπος.definition: turning out of the way. Adv. Erot. s.v

ἐκτυπόω.definition: model or work in relief; metaph. in Med., etc., form an image of a thing in . ., Pl.Tht.206d, cf. Lg.775d

ἐκφαίνω.definition: fut. Ion. in Luc.Syr.D.32: aor; of persons, bring to light, reveal, . . 19.104; produce him, Hdt.3.36; . . S.Ant.307, cf. OT329: c. part., Hdt.3.71; . . E.Hipp.428:—Pass., showed himself, came forth to view, Il.19.46,…

ἐκφατνίζω.definition: throw out of the manger: generally, throw; Med., eat out of the manger, Nic.Dam.p.3 D

ἐκφέρω.definition: fut. Hdt.3.71: Ion. aor; carry out a corpse for burial, Il.24.786, cf. Hdt.7.117, Antipho6.21 , etc.; also, cause death, Plot.1.4.8

ἐκφεύγω.definition: of persons accused, to be acquitted, Ar.V.157; c. gen., escape out of, Od.23.236; Epigr.Gr.1041.9; of things, Il.5.18: with Prep., APl.4.182

ἔκφημι.definition: speak out or forth, utter loudly:—Ep. only in Med., Od.10.246, cf. 13.308; A.R.1.439: later aor. 1 EM687.30

ἐκφθίνω.definition: in Hom. only in 3 plpf. Pass., the wine had all been consumed out of the ships, Od.9.163; 12.329; they have utterly perished, A.Pers.679 , 927

ἐκφλύζω.definition: or spirt out: c. acc. cogn., give vent to a groan, A.R.1.275

ἐκφοιτάω.definition: Ion. go out constantly, be in the; of things, to be spread abroad, Plu.Lyc.3

ἐκφορά.definition: carrying out, esp. of a corpse to; blabbing, betrayal of secrets, D.L.1.98

ἐκφορέω.definition: = carry out, as a corpse for burial; generally, carry out, Hdt.1.197, 9.116, Is.6.42 :—Med., take out with one, E.Cyc.234, etc.:— Pass., move forth, . . Il.19.360

ἐκφύω.definition: generate: mostly of the male, beget; rarely of the female, bear, S.OC984

ἐκχέω.definition: pour away: hence, spill, a vessel, Ar.Fr.306; Men.l.c.:—Pass., to be drained, PRyl.154.18

ἐκχιλόω.definition: cover all over with grass : land that bears nothing but grass, Paus. Gr.Fr.323

ἐκχολόω.definition: turn into bile, Herod.Med. in; Pass., to be charged with bile, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.15

ἐκχορεύω.definition: break out of the chorus: generally, break; Med., drive out of the chorus, E.Hel.381

ἐκχράω.definition: declare as an oracle, tell out; suffice, Hdt.8.70: impers., c. inf., how will it suffice him, how will he be content to . . ? Id.3.137

ἐκχυμόω.definition: extract juice from, Hp.Morb.2.47; in Pass., of the small veins, shed the blood and leave it extravasated under the skin, Id.Fract.11

ἔκχυσις.definition: outflow, Arist.Mete.354a26; pouring; effusion of pus, Erasistr. ap. Gal.8.318

ἐκχωνεύω.definition: melt down, coin anew, D.C.68.15 codd

ἐκχώννυμι.definition: raise a mound, Aq.Ez.17.17:—usu. in Pass; of a bay, to be filled up by the deposit of a river, v.l. ib.11

ἐκψύχω.definition: fut. lose consciousness, swoon; to be short of breath, gasp, Arist.Pr.886b14

ἐλαιόμελι.definition: sweet gum from the olive-tree, Dsc.1.31,etc

ἐλαιόω.definition: oil:—only Pass., to be oiled, Arist.HA605b20; bring to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.163B

ἐλαίωσις.definition: treatment with oil or reduction to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.215 B

ἐλασία.definition: = riding, X.Eq.Mag.4.4; striking from a die, Gloss

ἔλασμα.definition: metal beaten out, metal-plate; general name for probes and other surgical instruments, Gal.2.574; ibid.: esp. flat end of a probe, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.11.3

ἐλαστρέω.definition: Ep. and Ion. for . . they drove the teams, Il.18.543; Thgn.600; to drive about, of the Furies, E.IT971; in later Prose, D.H.1.23; row, Ion. part. Arr.Ind.32.9:—Pass., of ships, to be rowed, Hdt.2.158, 7.24; cf. · Hsch…

ἐλατήρ.definition: driver, esp. of horses; rower, Luc.Am.6, Nonn.D.39.306

ἐλαύνω.definition: Il.12.62, etc.: Ion. impf; with acc. omitted, intr., go in a chariot, drive, he whipped them on, Il.5.366, al., cf. S.El.734,739; he drove on over the waves, Il.13.27; travel the night through, Od.15.50; drive into th…

ἐλαφίς.definition: a bird, perh. heron or egret, Dionys.Av.2.11

ἐλάω.definition: Ion. poet. pres. for v. init

ἔλδομαι.definition: and poet. Verb, only pres. and impf., wish, long, c. inf., Il.13.638, Od.4.162, Pi.O.1.4: c. gen., long for, Od.5.210; eager to reach it, Il.23.122: c.acc., desire, Od.1.409, cf. Il.5.481: abs., Od.24.400:—Pass. only …

ἐλεαίρω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.24.23: aor. 1 A.R.4.1308, Sammelb.2134:—lengthd. form of take pity on, Il.6.407, Od.10.399, etc.—Ep. word, used by Ar.Eq.793 , Luc.Trag.305

ἐλεγχής.definition: worthy of reproof; of men, cowardly; reproachful, Nonn.D.40.35

ἐλέγχω.definition: test, bring to the proof, B.Fr.10.2; A.Ag.1351 ; Pl.Sph.242b : with subject. clause, . ., A.Ch.851, Ar.Eq.1232

ἐλεέω.definition: impf. Apollod.Com.4.1: aor. Ep; abs.,feel pity, Ar.Ach.706

ἐλελίζω.definition: Ep. redupl. of , rare in; Med. and Pass., move in coils or spires, of a serpent, Il.2.316; 11.39, cf. A.R.4.143; Ar.Fr.500

ἐλεφαίρομαι.definition: old Ep. Verb, perh. connected with; of the Nemean lion, he used to destroy them, Hes.Th.330

ἑλίκη.definition: the constellation of the Great Bear, from its revolving round the pole, Arat.37, A.R.3.1195

ἑλίκων.definition: thread spun from the distaff to the; a nine-stringed instrument, Aristid.Quint.3.3, Ptol.Harm.2.2

ἑλίσσω.definition: or (the latter more freq. in codd. of; generally, roll, roll life's stream along, Pi.I.8.15; of the chariot of Day, A.Pr.1092 ; . . E.Ph.3; roll the eddying dust, A.Pr.1085 ; of the Euripus, E.IT7, cf.1103 ; Id.HF868 …

ἑλκέω.definition: = drag about, tear asunder, in impf. . . Il.17.395: also in fut. and aor. ib.558; 22.336; he did violence to Leto, Od.11.580; Arat.638:—Pass., Il.22.62

ἑλκηθμός.definition: being carried off, violence suffered, Il.6.465

ἕλκημα.definition: that which is torn in pieces, prey, E.HF568

ἑλκητήρ.definition: one that drags, of a harrow, AP6.297

ἑλκοποιέω.definition: make wounds or sores: metaph., rip up old; make an incision in a tree, Gp.5.38

ἑλκυσμός.definition: attraction; esp. of idle fancy; dragging, in pl., Anon.Fig.p.156 S

ἑλκυστήρ.definition: instrument for drawing: surgeon's; as Adj., toil of dragging, Opp.H.5.20

ἕλκω.definition: Il.24.52, etc., impf; draw after one, . . Il.8.486; trail fetters after one, Hdt.3.129; let one's cloak trail behind, Ephipp.19 ; Archipp.45

ἕλκωμα.definition: sore, ulcer, Hp.Epid.3.7; part wounded, Thphr.HP9.2.1

ἐλλείχω.definition: lick in, take one's fill of, Com.Adesp.125 Meineke

ἐλπίζω.definition: Att. fut. LXXPs.43.7, Ep.Rom.15.12; of evils, look for, fear, in same constr., S.Tr.111 ; Id.Aj.799, cf. Lys.12.70; . . Ar.Av.956; Hdt.8.12; E.Ion348: with folld. by aor. subj., Hdt.1.77; Id.8.53

ἐλπίς.definition: hope, expectation; reason to expect or believe, Pl.Phd.67b, Lg.898d

ἐλύω.definition: roll round : only aor. 1 Pass; in later Ep., = wrap up, cover, shrouded in them, A.R.1.254; Opp.C.3.418, cf. H.2.89; A.R.3.1313

ἐμβαδόν.definition: Adv. by land, = Il.15.505; wading, Paus.10.20.8; a surface, area (opp

ἐμβαίνω.definition: fut. pf. Ep. part; go on, go quickly, says Antilochus to his horses, Il.23.403; advance! E.El.113

ἐμβάλλω.definition: fut. pf. aor. 2; of things, Thgn.551, X.Eq.6.7 , 9.9, cf. Il.19.394; E.IT1424; D.57.13, cf. X.Cyr.2.2.21; Id.An.7.1.12; Id.Cyr.8.1.38; throw food to . . , Thphr.Char.4.8; simply, lay or put in, put it into his hands, …

ἔμβαρος.definition: of weighty sense, Men.Phasm.Fr.3; pregnant, Gloss

ἐμβασιλεύω.definition: to be king in or among, c. dat., Od.15.413; Pi.N.7.38; A.R.1.173; Hes.Th.71, etc.; Iamb.Protr.20; Il.2.572: c. gen., Theoc.17.85

ἐμβάτης.definition: a kind of half-boot of felt; = Luc.JTr.41, Lib.Or.64.98, etc

ἔμβιος.definition: the moisture necessary to life, Thphr.CP1.1.3; Philostr.Im.1.24

ἐμβιόω.definition: fut. Philostr.Her.2.3:—live in; of plants, become established, Thphr.HP3.6.4; simply, take root, ib.6.7.3; Philostr. l.c

ἔμβλημα.definition: chased or embossed ornament used in decoration of plate, D.C.57.15, cf. Cic.Verr.4.17.37, etc

ἐμβόησις.definition: shouting, Aret.CA1.2, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.27, Antyll. ap. eund.6.6.5

ἔμβοθρος.definition: like a pit or hole, sunken, Thphr.HP9.3.1

ἐμβολή.definition: putting in, Thphr.Od.26 : esp. putting; insertion of a letter, Pl.Cra.437a

ἐμβρέμομαι.definition: Med., roar or bluster in, Il.15.627

ἔμβρωμα.definition: that which is eaten away; meal, snack, Ath.1.11c, cf. Sor.1.40

ἐμβύω.definition: stuff in, stop with a thing, Ar.V.128; Herod.2.82

ἐμέω.definition: metaph., throw up a flood of words, Eun.VSp.488 B

ἐμματέω.definition: put the finger down the throat to cause; implant a sting, of a bee, Nic.Th.809

ἐμμετρέω.definition: measure by or according to; simply, measure out, provide, PMasp.138iv1

ἐμμυέω.definition: initiate in: what, were you initiated at the great mysteries in that shabby coat? Ar.Pl.845 cod. R

ἐμπάζομαι.definition: used only in pres. , busy oneself about, take heed of, care for, c. gen., Od.1.271, al.; Il.16.50, cf. Od.2.201; 19.134; Timo50: once c. acc. pers., Od.16.422; also Coluth.38:—Ep. word, used in late Prose, Ael.Fr.325

ἐμπαίω.definition: strike in, stamp, emboss; intr., bursts in upon my soul, S.El.902

ἐμπάσσω.definition: Att. fut. in or on, Thphr.Lap.67; some powder, Pl.Ly.210a; Gal.11.134: in Hom. only metaph., weave rich patterns in a web of cloth, Il.3.126, cf. 22.441

ἐμπεριέχω.definition: encompass, surround, enclose; Astrol., blockade, Vett.Val.268.20

ἐμπερονάω.definition: fasten with a clasp, buckle on, in Med; Pass., of nails, to be fixed in, Ath.11.488b

ἐμπίμπρημι.definition: 3pl. impf. Th.6.94; also inf. Plu.Cor.26; part. Plb.1.53.4: impf. X.HG6.5.22: fut. Il.15.702, Ar.Th.749, 3pl. Tab.Heracl.1.145: aor. 1 Hom., etc.: aor. 1 Med. PTeb.61.289 , Q.S.5.485:—Pass., part. Hdt.1.19: fut. , Pau…

ἐμπίπτω.definition: fut. aor. Ep. (v; Geom., meet, of a line meeting another, Euc.1 Post.5, etc.; to be placed, Archim.Sph.Cyl.1.9; ibid

ἐμπλάζω.definition: drive about in:—hence in Pass., wander; metaph., Phld.Rh.1.376S

ἐμπλέκτης.definition: one who plaits hair, Gloss.:—fem. ib., EM528.5

ἐμπλήσσω.definition: intr., strike against, fall upon or into, c. dat., . . Od.22.469; Il.12.72; fall upon it, of a storm, Arat.423: abs., dash, A.R.1.1203, 2.602

ἐμπνέω.definition: poet. fut. E.Andr.555; abs., breathe in, inhale, Hp.Flat.4; but usu

ἔμπνοος.definition: contr. with the; of a flute, Sopat.10

ἐμποιέω.definition: put in, i.e. put their feet in the same tracks, X.Cyn.5.20; foist in, Hdt.7.6; D.H.4.62; simply, insert, opp. Schwyzer 412.3

ἐμπολάω.definition: deal or traffic in, Id.Ant.1037; purchase, buy, Id.OT1025, Ar.V.444, Pax367,563, etc.; S.Tr.250:—Med., E.Cret.7

ἐμπολέω.definition: Ion. and late form for Herod.6.63, Tz.H.1.820: Ion. part. Pass., or dub. sens. in Keil-PremersteinErster Bericht p.9

ἐμπόλημα.definition: matter of traffic, freight or; gain made by traffic, Thphr.Char.6.9

ἔμπολις.definition: belonging to the city or state, = Eup.137; one's fellow-citizen, S.OC1156, prob. for in ib.637

ἐμπόριον.definition: trading-station, mart, factory; market-centre for a district which had no SIG880.22

ἔμπρακτος.definition: within one's power to do, practicable; holding office, Cod.Just.1.2.24.1

ἐμπρήθω.definition: blow up, inflate, of the wind; burn, Il.9.589:—Pass., Ath.Med. ap. Orib.1.2.4; cf

ἐμπτοέω.definition: in Pass., to be stirred by passion, Procop.Gaz.p.156B

ἐμπυκάζω.definition: wrap up in:—Pass., his mind is shrouded, hard to make out, v.l. for in Mosch.1.15

ἔμπυος.definition: suffering from an abscess or; festering, suppurating, S.Ph.1378; Androm. ap. Gal.14.35; tents, Gal.19.97

ἐμφανής.definition: showing in itself, reflecting, of; visible to the eye, manifest

ἐμφορέω.definition: = to be borne about in or on; pour in, D.S.16.93; fill, Agath.1.1:— Med. and Pass., fill oneself with a thing, take one's fill or make much use of it, Hdt.1.55; to be filled full of, Duris27 J.; Hdn.4.11.3, Plu.2.1067…

ἔμφραγμα.definition: barrier, obstacle; wooden framework, casing, in pl., Ph.Bel.66.47

ἐμφύω.definition: Pass., with pf. and aor. 2 pf. subj. Thgn.396; grow in or on, Il.8.84; Hp.Aër.5; Hdt.2.156: hence of qualities, is implanted in him, Id.3.80; S.OT299; Id.OC1488; Id.Fr.949; E.Hipp.967; is set by nature on the body, Id…

ἐμψάω.definition: poet. wipe in or upon, Call.Fr.121

ἐμψίω.definition: feed with pap, prob. in A.Fr.51, cf. Bgk. ad Hippon.33

ἐναγής.definition: = under a curse or pollution; in S.OT656 , one who has invoked a curse upon his head

ἔναιμος.definition: with blood in one; red-blooded animals, Arist.HA489a30, PA690b11, al

ἐναιρέω.definition: capture in a place, Cret.aor.part. Pass. Leg.Gort.2.30

ἐναίρω.definition: also v.l. in Batr.274: aor. 2 Pi.Pae.6.114, E.Andr.1182 , S.Ant.871 ; poet. Pi.N.10.15, E.Supp.821 ; inf. Hes.Sc.329: later, aor. 1 Orph.A.666:—Med., Il.16.92: 3sg. aor. 1 5.43, Hes.Th.316:—Pass. :—poet. Verb , slay i…

ἐναιτέω.definition: claim a penalty, = Lat. petere, prob. in Supp.Epigr.1.161.56

ἐναιώρημα.definition: suspended matter in urine; outer part of an extension apparatus for broken limbs, Gal.18.581

ἐναπονίζω.definition: wash clean in a thing; Med., wash off from oneself in, Paus.9.30.8

ἐναποψύχω.definition: ease oneself in, euphem. for; cool off, PHolm.6.12

ἐναραρίσκω.definition: aor. 1 fit or fasten in; pf. intr., to be fitted in, 5.236; Arat.453

ἐνάργεια.definition: clearness, distinctness, vividness; Philos., clear and distinct perception, Epicur.Ep.1p.11U., al

ἐναργής.definition: visible, palpable, in bodily shape, esp; prominent, Aret.SD1.8

ἐναρδεύω.definition: irrigate, and one who irrigates, Gloss

ἔναρθρος.definition: jointed: of speech, articulate; strong in limb, Aret.SD2.5

ἐναρίζω.definition: Il.1.191, etc.: impf. A.Ag.1644; Ep. : fut. Il.20.339: aor.Ep. and Lyr. 22.323, Pi.N.6.52, later Lyc.486, AP7.226 :—Med., aor. Opp.C.2.20:—Pass., S.Tr.94 : aor. pf. :—strip a slain foe of his arms , c. dupl. acc., . .…

ἐνασκέω.definition: train or practise in a thing; Pass., to be wrought in it, J.AJ3.7.5

ἐναττικίζω.definition: the nightingales sing in this place just as in Attica, Philostr.Her.Prooem

ἐναύλιος.definition: inside the court; the inner life, Zos.Alch.p.229B

ἐνδάκνω.definition: bite into, seize with the teeth; metaph., of sharp things, fix themselves firm in, Apollod.Poliorc.145.9; of mustard, to be pungent, Nic.Fr.70.16

ἐνδακρύω.definition: weep in or with, suffuse them with tears, A.Ag.541

ἐνδεής.definition: neut. pl. :—wanting or; abs., in want, in need, X.HG6.1.3 codd., etc

ἐνδείκνυμι.definition: or fut. mark, point; law-term, inform against, Id.Ap.32b: abs., Isoc.18.20; Pl.Lg.856c, cf. And.1.8, etc.; IG22.1128.18; ib.12.62.53 :— Med., Plu.Sol.24:—freq. in Pass., Antipho5.9; Lys.6.15, OGI669.45 ; D.21.182

ἐνδεκάζω.definition: celebrate the tenth of the month, cited by Harp.fr.D.58.[40]

ἐνδέμω.definition: wall up, Hdt.3.117; build in a place, Theoc.17.82:—Med., build or make for oneself in, Nic.Th.419

ἔνδεσις.definition: binding on, of the point of; swaddling, Sor.1.84

ἐνδεύω.definition: Aeol.for , to be wanting, IG12.6; soak or dye in, Nic.Al.414

ἐνδέχομαι.definition: Ion. fut. take upon; in Hdt. freq. give ear to, believe, mostly with a neg., . . 5.106; 4.25, cf. 3.73, 7.237: c. inf., believe that . ., 3.115

ἐνδέω.definition: fut. , bind in, on or to; metaph., . . entangled me in it, Il.2.111, cf. S.OC526 ; Hdt.1.11:—Pass., Id.3.19; Id.9.16; Plb.6.17.8; Id.20. 11.10; i.e. in debt, Id.13.1.3; to have the government secured, Id.9.23.2:—Med.,…

ἐνδιάω.definition: stay in the open air: generally; trans., shepherds drove their sheep afield, Theoc.16.38

ἐνδιήκω.definition: pervade, as the essence pervades the individuals of a class, S.E.M.8.41

ἐνδιόω.definition: Dor., pf. part. perh. established, of plants, Tab.Heracl.1.121; perh. cf

ἐνδοτέρω.definition: Adv.Comp.of more within, quite within; of Time, within a certain limit, sooner, Hp.Fract.33

ἐνδουπέω.definition: fall in with a heavy sound, Od.12.443; 15.479

ἐνδρομή.definition: air played during the pentathlon, Plu.2.1140d

ἐνδρομίς.definition: a sort of high shoe, worn by; Adj., used in the foot-race, GDI2517.11

ἐνδύω.definition: c. acc. rei vel loci, go into; enter, press into, c. acc., Il.19.367; thou wilt enter the contest , 23.622; Pl.R.620c; Id.Lg.642b; Id.Tht.169c; also . . Ar.V.1020, Arist.HA609b21; enter upon it, undertake it, X.Cyr.8.…

ἐνέζομαι.definition: sit in or upon, Arist.Pr.881b36; have one's seat or abode in, c. acc. loci, A.Pers.140

ἐνείλησις.definition: wrapping, bandaging, Herod.Med. ap; confinement of intestinal gases, Ruf. ap.eund.8.24.9

ἔνειμι.definition: c. dat. pl., to be among, Thgn.1135, Hdt.3.81, al.; 1 Ep.Cor.6.5

ἐνέπω.definition: lengthd. both forms in Hom. and Pi; c. acc. et inf., bid one do so and so, Pi.P.9.96, S.OT350, OC932

ἐνέργημα.definition: action, activity, operation; realized object, Plot.6.8.16, cf.6.9.2

ἐνεργμός.definition: a way of playing on the lyre; peg on the for tuning the strings, Euphron. ap.EM340.3

ἐνερείδω.definition: intr., lie in or on, adherent to . ., Dsc.3.23:—Med., A.R.1.428

ἐνετήρ.definition: clyster-syringe, Cass.Fel.48; siege-engine of war for hurling projectiles, Ph.Bel.91.45, 100.18

ἐνεύδω.definition: sleep in or on, . . Od.20.95, cf. 3.350, al., Theoc.5.10; D.L.6.22

ἐνεύναιος.definition: on which one sleeps, . . a skin to sleep on, Od.14.51; for want of bed-furniture, 16.35; bed-clothes, Hierocl.p.25A

ἐνέχω.definition: hold or keep fast within; Pass., with fut. and aor. Med. , to be held, caught, entangled in, c. dat., X.An.7.4.17; Pl.La.183e

ἐνέψημα.definition: a thing boiled or infused, Aret.CA1.1

ἐνέψω.definition: boil in or among, Aret.CA1.1: pf. Pass., ib.6: aor. 1 Pass., . . Nic.Al.71

ἐνηβάω.definition: spend one's youth in, Longus3.13; of plants, flourish in, Cratin.325, cf. Nic.Fr.85.2

ἐνῆμαι.definition: used as pf. of to be seated in, Od.4.272, cf. Theoc.22.44; . . E.Fr.795

ἐνηχέω.definition: to be resonant, Aret.SA1.6: c. dat., ring in; teach by voice, word of mouth, Eustr.in EN112.19

ἐνήχημα.definition: a sound in one's ears, Iamb.VP15.65 codd

ἔνηχος.definition: sounding within, of wind-instruments, opp; c. gen., acquainted, conversant with, LXXSi.prol.9

ἐνθάκησις.definition: sitting in, a twofold seat in the sun, i.e. both at morn and evening, S.Ph.18

ἔνθετος.definition: capable of being put in; grafted, Hp.Nat.Puer.26

ἐνθρῴσκω.definition: aor. 2 Ep. in, on, or among, c. dat., Il.21.233; 15.623; 5.161, cf. 20.381; Pi.P.3.37; E.El.327; kicked him on the hip, Od.17.233; D.C.74.14: metaph., Orac.Chald. ap. Dam.Pr.182

ἐνθύμημα.definition: thought, piece of reasoning; meaning, sense, opp. Olymp.in Mete.4.23

ἐνιαύω.definition: sleep among, Od.15.557, cf. 9.187; sleep in, Bion1.72

ἐνιζάνω.definition: sit or settle in or on, Il.20.11; offood, Alciphr.1.22, cf. Lib.Or.60.11: metaph. of and its object, Plot.4.6.3

ἑνίζω.definition: to be a partisan of the One, i.e. teach a; treat as a unity, Plot.6.9.6:—Pass., ibid

ἐνίημι.definition: fut. Th.4.115: aor. Ep; implant, inspire, c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Il.20.80; 17.570; 16.449; E.Ba.851; involve them in expense, PAmh.2.133.9 :—Pass., introduced from without, Plot.6.3.23

ἐνικλάω.definition: poet. for , break off: metaph., is wont to frustrate what I devise, Il.8.408, cf. 422; Call.Jov.90; Id.Aet.3.1.22; A.R.3.307

ἐνίπτω.definition: fut. Il.7.447: aor. 2.245; after Hom., = tell, announce, Pi.P.4.201, cf. Nonn.D.27.59. cf

ἐνίσσω.definition: Ep. collat. form of attack, reproach, Il.15.198; 22.497; 24.238: also generally, maltreat, Od.24.161:—Pass., ib.163

ἐνίστημι.definition: causal in pres., fut.and aor. 1 Act., and; in Law, institute an heir, PMasp.151.75

ἐννεύω.definition: nod or make signs to, Ar.Fr.75, cf. Luc.DMeretr.12.1; . . ask him by signs what . ., Ev.Luc.1.62

ἕννυμι.definition: Med. and Pass., c. acc. rei only, clothe oneself in, put on, wear, Od.23.115; 15.331; freq. of armour, Il.14.383, etc.; of tall shields which covered the whole person, ib.372; shafts clad with brass at their point, 15…

ἑνόζυγος.definition: of single pairs of gladiators matched with beasts, IGRom.4.1632

ἐνοίκειος.definition: contained in a house: furniture, contents of a house, Rev.Et.Gr. 32.171

ἐνοκλάζω.definition: squat upon, of a dog, Philostr.Jun.Im.3

ἐνόπλιος.definition: contest in arms, of a race of war- chariots, SIG802A 10

ἑνοποιέω.definition: combine in one, unite, Arist.de; unify, Dam.Pr.391:—391:—Pass., Procl.in Prm.p.541 S

ἐνοράω.definition: fut. Iamb.in Nic.p.38P.: aor; look at, behold, Arist.Fr.153; Plu.Publ.6; Paus.4.8.2

ἔνορκος.definition: having sworn, bound by oath; = included in a treaty, Th.2.72

ἐνόρνυμι.definition: aor. 1 Ep. aor. 2 Pass. only two tenses used by Hom.:—arouse, stir up in a person, Il.6.499; 15.62; 2.451; 11.544; Alc.Supp.23.12; . . E.Supp.713:—Pass., arise in or among, Il.1.599

ἐνορούω.definition: leap in or upon, usu. of an assault, c. dat., . . Il.16.783; . . . . 10.486: abs., 11.217; prob. in Hp.Cord.2; of fish, Opp.H.2.516

ἐνούσιος.definition: Adv. on the security of one's property, CPR40.15

ἐνρήγνυμι.definition: break into:—Pass., discharge itself into; intr. in pf. part. Act. broken, IG11.199B90

ἐνσάττω.definition: stuff in, of one eating sausages, Alciphr.3.7

ἔνσειμι.definition: Cret. for enter, 3sg. pres. subj. Leg.Gort. 5.36

ἔνσιτος.definition: public guest, a title of honour at; fed, replete, Hippiatr.111

ἐνσκίμπτω.definition: poet. Ep. and Lyr. form of

ἐνσοβέω.definition: step proudly in, Philostr.VA6.10; agitate:— Pass., agitation, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.127

ἐνστάζω.definition: fut. drop in or into, Ar.V.702, Pi.P.9.63 ; B.12.229; Ph.2.470:—Pass., is instilled into thee, Od.2.271; Hdt.9.3, cf. Dsc.Eup.1.35, Plu.Ages.11, Paus.4.32.4

ἐνστηρίζω.definition: fix or press in, Hp.VC21: metaph., Plot.3.5.2:—Pass., it stuck fast in earth, Il.21.168; of Delos, Call.Del.13:—the Med. in A.R.4.1518

ἐνστρέφω.definition: turn in:—Med., turn or; c. acc. loci, visit them, f.l. in E.Ion300

ἐντάγιον.definition: order for delivery, esp. requisition by; receipt, PSI1.36 , etc

ἐντανύω.definition: poet. and Ion. for stretch tight, of; stretch or strain tight with cords or straps, cover it with stretched straps, Hdt.5.25

ἐντάσσω.definition: Att. insert or register in; arrange light-armed troops and hoplites alternately, Ael.Tact.31.3, Arr.Tact.26.6: generally, insert men alternately, ib.25.4

ἐντείνω.definition: stretch or strain tight, esp. of any operation; Hdt.5.25 :—more freq. Pass., . . is hung on tight- stretched straps. Il.5.728; was strongly lined inside with tight-stretched straps, 10.263; so expected to find the bri…

ἐντήκω.definition: pour in while molten, D.S.2.8; Pass., with pf. Act. to be dissolved in, Aët.9.42

ἐντίθημι.definition: fut. poet. aor. 1 inf; metaph., Thgn.430; Pherecr.146.6; Pl.Lg.800c; D.3.33; inspire fear, X.An.7.4.1, etc.; Plot.4.7.8:—so in Med., thou hast stored up wrath in thy heart, Il.6.326; Od.11.102; opp. Il.9.639; PMag.Lon…

ἔντμημα.definition: cut in a thing, incision, notch, X.Cyn.2.7

ἐντομή.definition: slit, groove, Hp.Art.33,47; in insects; hewing of masonry, Th.1.93

ἔντομος.definition: cut in pieces, esp. in neut. pl; insects, Arist.HA487a33, cf. 523b13, Ant.Lib.4.7

ἔντονος.definition: of persons, sinewy, v.l. for; Subst. dub.l. for Pl.Lg.945c.—Freq. confounded with

ἐντρέπω.definition: turn about, Hdt.7.211; mostly metaph., make one turn, put him to shame, 1 Ep.Cor.4.14, Ael.VH3.17, S.E.P.3.135, D.L.2.29

ἐντρέχω.definition: aor. run in, be active in: hence; to be current among, Arat.100

ἐντριβής.definition: metaph. from the touchstone, proved by; beaten track, App.Hann.4

ἐντρίχωμα.definition: edges of the eyelids, eyelashes; hair-sieve, also Plu.2.912e

ἐντροπαλίζομαι.definition: Pass., Frequentat. of only pres. part., often turning round, Il.6.496; esp. of men retreating with their face to the enemy, 11.547, cf. 17.109, 21.492, Q.S.12.583

ἐντροπή.definition: turning towards: only metaph. (cf; humiliation, LXXPs.34.26, al

ἐντύνω.definition: fut. Lyc.734: aor. 1; c. acc., make one ready, urge him on, Thgn.196, cf. Pi.O.3.28: also c. inf., urge to do a thing, Id.P.9.66, N.9.36

ἐντυπόω.definition: carve or mould in or upon; metaph., Longin.10.6

ἐντυρόω.definition: in Pass., to be turned into cheese, prob. in Nic.Al.364

ἐντύφω.definition: fut. smoke as one does wasps; frost-bitten, EM458.42

ἐνυφαίνω.definition: weave in as a pattern; weave in a place, Leg.Gort.2.51

ἐνωπή.definition: face, countenance, used by Hom. only in dat. as Adv., before the face, openly, Il.5.374, [21.510]; later Nic.Th.227

ἐξαγγελία.definition: secret information sent out to the; expression, of style, Longin.Rh.p.186H

ἐξαγγέλλω.definition: tell out, proclaim, make known, freq. with; express, Hermog.Id.2.5:—Pass., to be expressed, Arist.Po.1460b11; Ti.Locr.102e

ἐξάγγελος.definition: messenger who brings out news from; on the Greek stage, messenger who told what was doing in the house or behind the scenes ; first used by Aeschylus, Philostr.VS1.9

ἐξαγίζω.definition: drive out as accursed, . . A.Ag.641: or perh. fr. taken as victims from many homes

ἐξαγορεύω.definition: fut. Epic.Alex.Adesp.2.55: aor. supplied by fut. and pf. by out, make known, declare, Od.11.234; betray a secret or mystery, Hdt.2.170; Id.9.89; Luc.Pisc.33; confess, LXXLe.5.5, Plu.2.168d: abs., Rhetor.inCat.Cod. Ast…

ἐξάγω.definition: pf. D.42.19, PHib.1.34.10 (iii B; of persons, mostly c. gen. loci, Od.22.458, 23.372, Il.5.353; ib.35: with . ., Od.8.106, 20.21; Hdt.4.148, al.; having brought her out from Argos, Il.13.379; bring out of prison, rele…

ἐξαγωγή.definition: leading out of troops, X.Eq.Mag.4.9; drawing out of a ship from shallows, Hdt.4.179

ἐξᾴδω.definition: sing out, sing one's last song, of the swan; sing the of a chorus, Plot.6.9.8

ἑξαετής.definition: or six years old; of six years, Plu.Pyrrh.26. Adv. for six years, Od.3.115; cf

ἐξαθρέω.definition: look at carefully, dub. in Thesp. ap. Chrysipp.Stoic.2.55

ἐξαιμάσσω.definition: Att. make quite bloody; metaph., open one's griefs afresh, D.H.6.81

ἐξαίνυμαι.definition: take out or away, took out , Od.15.206: in Il. always in phrase animam eripuit, 5.155, al.; Nic.Al.272

ἐξαίρεσις.definition: taking out the entrails of victims; removal, purgation, Porph.Abst.2.43

ἐξαιρέω.definition: fut. later D.H.7.56, etc.: aor. 2; Med., take out for oneself, from his quiver, Il.8.323; their large sails, X.HG1.1.13; discharge their cargoes, Hdt.4.196; X.An.5.1.16; Th.8.90: abs., Syngr. ap. D.35.13, etc.:—Pass.,…

ἐξαίρω.definition: Ep. Hom. , also in Ion; seemingly intr., rise from the ground, of a bird, D.S.2.50; start, Plb.2.23.4, cf. LXXNu.2.9

ἐξακέομαι.definition: heal completely, Hp.Vict.3.67: hence, make; c. acc., appease, Il.4.36, cf. Od.3.145; quench, D.C.60.9; make up for, X.Cyr.8.2.22; Iamb.Myst.1.11

ἐξακούω.definition: hear or catch a sound, esp. from a distance; understand in a certain sense, Id.7.89

ἐξαλαόω.definition: blind utterly, Od.11.103; make blind and useless, Opp.C.3.228

ἐξαλαπάζω.definition: sack, storm, Il.4.40, 1.129, etc.; also, empty a city of its inhabitants, clear it out, so as to plant new settlers in it, Od.4.176: generally, destroy utterly, Il.13.813, 20.30: metaph., Theoc.2.85.—Ep. word, used by…

ἐξάλλομαι.definition: fut. LXXMi.2.12: aor; start from its socket, be dislocated, of a limb, Hp.Art.46; of a broken bone, Plu.2.341b; of wheels, start from the axle, X.Cyr.7.1.32

ἐξάλμυρος.definition: having lost its saltness, of earth, Thunell Sitologen papyri 1viii 11

ἑξαμερής.definition: in six parts, of the hexameter, Orph.Fr.356

ἐξαναβαίνω.definition: get to the top of, Artem.2.28; Epigr.Gr.782

ἐξαναβρύω.definition: causal of foreg., cause happiness to spring forth from the earth, A.Eu.925

ἐξαναδύομαι.definition: aor. 2 Act. rise out of, emerge; escape from, c. gen., Plu.Sert.12: c. acc., Thgn.1124; Orac. ap. Paus.4.12.4

ἐξαναζέω.definition: boil up with: c. acc. cogn., metaph., . . will let such fury boil forth, A.Pr.372

ἐξαναφέρω.definition: bear up, of buoyant sea-water; exhibit the form of a spear, Plu.2.563a

ἐξανεμόω.definition: blow out with wind, inflate:—Pass., to be; Pass., of corn, to be parched by wind, 'wind- bitten', Thphr.HP8.10.3

ἐξανθίζω.definition: deck as with flowers, paint in various; Med., gather flowers, Plu.2.661f

ἐξανίημι.definition: poet. impf. A.R.4.622: fut; c. gen., send forth from, Pi.P.4.99; E.Ba.762; Id.HF625

ἐξανύω.definition: conquer, App.Ill.15; of Time and Distance, bring to an end, finish, accomplish, S.Tr.1022 ; E.Med.649 ; Id.Ph.163 , Tr.232 , IT897 : abs. . finish one's way to a place, arrive at it, or . ., Hdt.6.139,7.183: also c. a…

ἐξαπατάω.definition: Ep. iter. Ar.Pax1070 :—Pass., fut. Pl.Grg.499c; but in pass. sense, X.An.7.3.3:—deceive or beguile, deceive thoroughly, . . Il.9.371, cf. Od.9.414, Pi.O.1.29, Hdt.1.153, Ar.V.901, etc.; Id.Pax1099 ; D.21.204; seduce a…

ἐξαπαφίσκω.definition: Ep., = Hes.Th.537: aor. Od.14.379; subj. 23.79; part. h.Ap.379, h.Ven.38, E.Ion704 , Alex.Aet.3.19, etc.: Hom. also has 3sg. aor. opt. Med. in act. sense, Il.9.376, 14.160: later aor. 1 h.Ap.376, Q.S.1.137, Opp.H.3.94

ἐξάπλωσις.definition: opening out, of roots, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.12; explanation, Erot.Prooem

ἐξαποβαίνω.definition: step out of, Od.12.306; A.R.3.199, etc

ἐξαπόλλυμι.definition: Pass., with pf. 2 aor. 2 utterly out of, c. gen., Il.6.60; 18.290; Od.20.357; A.Ag.528: abs., perish utterly, Hdt.4.173, S.Fr.236

ἐξαπολογία.definition: title of three speeches of Antipho, second defence, rejoinder

ἐξάπτω.definition: fasten from or to; metaph., let prayers fall from one's mouth, E.Or.383; consider actions as dependent upon chance, Plu.Sull.6; continue the narrative, D.L.8.50; dependent on it, Ti.Locr.102e

ἐξαράσσω.definition: c. acc. pers., assail him furiously with abuse, Ar.Nu.1373

ἐξαρθρέω.definition: dislocate the joints of; intr., to be dislocated, Hp.Art.29; suffer from dislocations, ib.8, 53

ἐξαρπάζω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.708: aor.1 Hom; tear out, . . Ar.Eq.708; tear off, Asclep. ap. Gal.12.418

ἐξάρτημα.definition: that which is suspended from; that which is attached or dependent, Dam.Pr.130

ἐξάρτησις.definition: attachment of parts of the body one; suspension of a weight, Sor.1.72

ἐξάρχω.definition: begin, take the lead in, initiate, c. gen; hold office, Polem.Cyn.18; rule, c. gen., Eustr.in EN2.32

ἐξάρχων.definition: ruler, president, Müller-Bees Inschriften der jüdischen Katakombe am Monteverde No.14

ἐξαύξω.definition: increase, Thphr.CP1.22.1:—Pass., grow too fast, Id.HP6.6.6

ἐξαφαιρέω.definition: take away:—Med., Od.22.444, cf. S.El.1157; Trag.Adesp.296; f.l. in D.8.42

ἐξαφύω.definition: draw forth, . . Od.14.95: poet. aor., Opp.H.1.573: Ep. fut. 3pl., Hsch

ἔξεδρος.definition: away from home, opp; c. gen., out of, away from, E.IT80: metaph., insensate words, Id.Hipp.935

ἐξεθισμός.definition: change of habit, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.1.7

ἐξειλύω.definition: unfold:—Pass., of serpents gliding along the ground, Theoc.24.17

ἔξειμι.definition: come forth to apply the test, S.Ph.98; but, submit to the test, Id.Fr.105; . . E.Fr.334

ἐξελαιόω.definition: make into oil, Thphr.CP6.8.1:—Pass., become oily, ib.6.7.4

ἐξελαύνω.definition: fut. Hdt.4.148, 5.63, IG12.39.4: pf; drive out horses, etc., out of the ranks of the Trojans, Il.5.324, cf. 10.499; E.Ph.1190:—Med., drive out one's horses, Theoc.24.119 ; lead out an army, Hdt.1.76, 7.38; A.R.1.987; …

ἐξέλκω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.365 : aor. 1 inf. Id.Pax315, 506:—Pass., Hdt.2.70:— draw, drag out, Il.23.762: c. gen. loci, Od.5.432 ; . . E.Hec.544; rescue from slavery, Pi.P.1.75; of a lame man, S.Ph.291: abs., without of one wounded, …

ἐξεμέω.definition: pf. Aristid.Or.50.5 (v.l; abs., vomit, be sick, Ar.Ra.11

ἐξεναρίζω.definition: strip or spoil a foe slain in fight; kill, slay, Od.11.273; Il.6.30, cf. Hes.Th.289, B.5.146, Lyc.50, etc.—In Hom. more freq. than the simple Verb

ἐξερεείνω.definition: c. acc. rei, inquire into, Od.10.14; c. acc. pers., inquire after, . . 23.86; inquire of, A.R.4.1250: abs., make inquiry, Il.9.672, etc.:—Med., 10.81

ἐξερείπω.definition: strike off, Pi.P.4.264; more freq. intr. in aor. 2 inf. to earth, Il.14.414; the mane streaming downwards from the yoke-cushion, 17.440; letting their necks fall on the ground, Hes.Sc.174; fall down, Id.Th.704.—Mostly…

ἐξερέω.definition: Att. contr. fut. of :—I will speak out, tell out, utter aloud, Hom. always abs. in sg., Il.8.286, 12.215, Od.9.365, al.; in tmesi, Il.1.204, 233, al.: c. acc. in Trag., S.OT800, cf. 219, etc.: c. dupl. acc., Id.El.984…

ἐξέρομαι.definition: Ion. fut. aor. 2; c. acc. rei, inquire into a thing, Od.13.127; so also . . will inquire concerning him, what he is now about, S.Ph.439

ἐξερύω.definition: Ion. aor.1 Ep. and also :—draw out of, . . Il.5.112; . . Od.22.386, cf. Hdt.1.141; Il.16.505; snatch out of, 23.870; but . . by the foot, 10.490; draw out, 13.194; tear out, Od.18.87; Hdt.2.38

ἐξέρχομαι.definition: fut. supplies the fut., also impf. aor. 2 the only tense used in Hom.:-go or come out of, c. gen.loci, Il.22.237,413,417; 10.140; etc., A.Ch.663, S.El.778, etc.; . . Hdt.8.75, 9.12, S.OC37, etc.; . . E.Ph.476; of an a…

ἐξερωέω.definition: swerve from the course, of shy horses, Il.23.468; Theoc.25.189

ἐξευπορέω.definition: supply abundantly; abs., find a way out, ib.861b.—The form in X.An.5.6.19, is prob. f.l. for

ἐξεύρεσις.definition: searching out, search, Hdt.1.67; finding out, invention, ib.94

ἐξευρίσκω.definition: fut. aor. 2 Med; seek out, search after, Id.7.119,5.33

ἐξέψω.definition: boil thoroughly, Hdt.4.61:—Pass., to be boiled out, v.l. in Arist.Mete.384a2

ἐξηγέομαι.definition: to be leader of, c. gen. pers; c. acc. pers., lead, govern, in Th., 1.76; ib.71

ἐξηθέω.definition: filter out, purify, in Pass., Arist.Pr.967a15, Thphr.CP6.13.1

ἐξήκω.definition: to have reached a certain point; of prophecies, dreams, etc., to have come to an accomplishment, turn out true, Hdt.1.120, 6.80; S.OT1182; of magical operations, succeed, PMag.Par.1.1273

ἐξηχέω.definition: sound forth, LXXJl.3.14, Nech. ap; utter senseless sounds, of idiots, Polem.Phgn.51

ἔξηχος.definition: rudely sounding: hence, absurd, stupid, Porph.Chr.35, EM696.39

ἐξίημι.definition: send out, let one go out; intr., of rivers, discharge themselves, Hdt.1.6 , al., Th.4.103

ἐξιθύνω.definition: make straight, Il.15.410; direct aright, A.R.1.562

ἐξικνέομαι.definition: poet. aor. Il.9.479, augm; come to as a suppliant, c. acc. pers., Od.13.206, 20.223, Pi.P.11.35; Ant.Lib.38.2

ἐξιόω.definition: clean from rust, Arr.Epict.4.11.13; make poisonous, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.104

ἐξιπόω.definition: press or squeeze out, Hp.Art.50; dry thoroughly, Aristid.Or.36.69:—Pass., prob.l. in Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.44 B

ἐξισόω.definition: make equal or even, bring to a level with; Pass., is levelled, equalized, i.e. resolved in harmony, S.El.1072 ; lit., levelled, J.BJ5.3.5

ἐξισχύω.definition: have strength enough, be able; c. gen., fate prevailing over the children, Ael.VH6.13, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.71D

ἐξίσχω.definition: intr., stand out, project, Paus.5.12.1; prominent eyes, Hp.Prog.2, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.27; of bones, Aret.SA2.8

ἔξογκος.definition: prominent, Plu.Fr.inc.149, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.187 D

ἐξοδεία.definition: prob. for expedition, Plb.4.54.3; procession from the shrines, OGI90.42

ἐξοδία.definition: Ion. marching out, expedition; journey, PSI4.406.27

ἐξόζω.definition: intr., smell, smell; c. gen., smell of a thing, Thphr.Od.20

ἐξοίχομαι.definition: to have gone out, to be quite gone, Il.6.379,384, S.OC867; Pl.Com.69.11: metaph., Antipho Soph.49; Pl.R.503c

ἐξόλλυμι.definition: and fut. aor. 1 pf; Med., with pf. 2 perish utterly, Emp.11.3, S.Tr.84, Ar.Pax366, Pl.l.c., etc.; . . Ar.Pax483: opt. in imprecations, Id.Fr.105; Alex.120

ἐξομματόω.definition: open the eyes of; metaph., make clear or plain, A.Pr.499

ἐξονομαίνω.definition: name, speak of by name, Il.3.166; . . name, tell it, Od.6.66, cf. h.Ven.252; SIG527.122

ἐξονυχίζω.definition: try a thing's smoothness by drawing the; deprive of the base of the petal, Orib.5.33.1; of lilies, in Pass., Aët.1.115

ἐξοπτάω.definition: bake thoroughly; metaph., of love, S.Fr.474.3

ἐξοράω.definition: see from afar:—Pass; have the appearance, Hp.Morb.2.68

ἐξοργιάζω.definition: excite to mystic frenzy; intr., become frenzied, ib.p.26 K

ἐξόριος.definition: out of the bounds of one's; Subst., , exile, Marcellin.Vit. Thuc.47, Eust.1161.35

ἐξόριστος.definition: expelled, banished; put beyond the borders, of the dead body of a criminal, . . Din.1.77

ἐξορμάω.definition: send forth, send to war, A.Pers.46, E.IT1437; intr., like Pass., set out, start, esp. in haste, Od.12.221; X.An.5.7.17: c. gen., set out from, E.Tr.1131, etc.: metaph., break out, S.Tr.1089

ἔξορμος.definition: sailing from a harbour, c. gen; issuing forth, dub. l. in Arist.PA694a23

ἐξοφέλλω.definition: increase exceedingly, offered higher and higher dowry, Od.15.18

ἐξυμενίζω.definition: strip off the skin or membrane, Dsc.2.76.1; Archig. ap. Aët.16.48

ἐξυπανίστημι.definition: only in intr. aor. 2, a weal started up from under the skin of the back, Il.2.267, cf. Pythag. ap. Porph.VP40

ἐξυπτιάζω.definition: turn a person quite on the back; intr., lie back, of the horns of wild cattle, Id.HA499a7

ἔξω.definition: with Verbs of motion, out or out of, Od.14.526; Hdt.1.10; Pl.Phdr.247b; D.18.323; Luc.Alex.38, etc

ἐξωθέω.definition: aor. 1 , thrust out, force; put forth painful words, break forth into cruel words, S.Ph.1142

ἐξωμίας.definition: one with arms bare to the shoulder, Luc.Vit.Auct.7

ἐξωριάζω.definition: leave out of thought, neglect, f.l. for A.Pr.17

ἔξωσις.definition: putting out, displacement, Hp.Art.46; thrust, Marcellin.Puls.99

ἐξώστρα.definition: stage-machine identified with the; bridge thrust out from the besiegers' tower against the walls of the besieged place, Lat. exostra, Veget.de Re Milit.4.21

ἐξώφορος.definition: brought out, published; tending outwards, Marcellin.Puls.65

ἐπαγάλλομαι.definition: Pass., glory in, exult in, c. dat., Il.16.91, cf. Q.S.7.327, Tryph.671; Crates Theb.4; Them.Or.11.151c; Artem.3.31; X.Oec.4.17

ἐπαγείρω.definition: gather together, collect, of things, Il.1.126:—Pass., of men, assemble, Od.11.632, cf. Pi.P.9.54

ἐπαγοράζω.definition: purchase a title to the next vacancy of a priesthood, SIG1014.17

ἐπάγω.definition: set on, urge on, as hunters do dogs, Od.19.445, cf. X.Cyn.10.19:— in Med., ib.6.25

ἐπαγωγή.definition: bringing on or to; bringing in to one's aid, introduction, Id.3.100, cf. 82 ; introduction of food through the gullet, Arist.Spir.483a9

ἐπαέξω.definition: make to grow, prosper, Od.14.65:— Pass., increase, grow, Semon.7.85 , Nic.Th.449

ἐπαιάζω.definition: cry over, mourn over; join in the wail, Bion1.2, etc.; Luc.Luct.20

ἐπαιγίζω.definition: rush upon, twice in Hom. of a stormy wind, . . Il.2.148; . . Od.15.293; Alciphr.3.42: metaph., AP5.285 : c. dat., rush over, of a stream that has burst its banks, Opp.C.2.125: c. acc., of the dolphin, Id.H.2.583

ἐπαινέω.definition: Aeol. Simon.5.19; Lacon; praise, commend in any way , or Alc.37A, Hdt.3.34,6.130; E.Hipp.264; commend one for a thing, but in this case the thing is always a neut. Pron. or Adj., A.Pr.342 ; S.Aj.1381, cf. Pl.Smp.222a;…

ἐπαίρω.definition: Ion. and poet. Hdt.1.204 and always in; lift, raise, 10.80; S.Ph.889; Id.OT1276 codd.; E.Tr.99 ; Ar.V.996; Amphis l.c.; SIG1109.24; IG3.1132; D.18.291; opp. Plu.Luc.3:—Med., didst lift and put me to thy breast, A.R.3.…

ἐπαιτέω.definition: beg as a mendicant, Id.OC1364, cf. E.Rh.715: abs., Vett.Val.68.30, Luc.Asin.35

ἐπακούω.definition: fut. ib.Ge.30.33, later Psalm.Solom.18.3:-hear, c. acc. rei, of the Sun, Il.3.277, cf. Od.11.109; prov., as thou speakest, so wilt thou be answered, Il.20.250; Hes.Op.448; Ar.Eq.1080: c. acc. rei et gen. pers., Od.19.…

ἐπακρίζω.definition: reach the top of a thing, he reached the farthest point in deeds of blood, of Orestes, A.Ch.932

ἐπαλάομαι.definition: wander about or over, Od.4.81; ib.83: subj. aor. 15.401

ἐπαλαστέω.definition: to be full of wrath at a thing, Od.1.252, cf. A.R.3.369,557

ἐπάλειψις.definition: painting over of colours; smearing over, anointing, EM69.41

ἐπαλέξω.definition: Ep. Verb, defend, succour, Il.8.365; ward off, keep off, Il.20.315

ἐπαληθεύω.definition: prove true, substantiate, verify; prove one's right to, Ph.2.6, 263

ἐπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. change over: once in Hom; intr., alternate, interlocking teeth, Arist.PA661b18; of leaves, dub. in Thphr.HP4.6.10

ἐπαμαξεύω.definition: = traverse with cars, . . marked with the tracks of wheels, S.Ant.251

ἐπαμβατήρ.definition: poet. for one who mounts upon, assailant: metaph., of leprous eruptions, A.Ch.280

ἐπαμείβω.definition: exchange, barter, Il.6.230; Orph.A.422:—Med., come one after another, come in turn to, Il.6.339; Archil.9.9

ἐπαμύνω.definition: come to aid, succour, Il.6.361; ward off, v.l. for in AP5.6

ἐπανάγω.definition: bring up: hence; stir up, excite, Hdt.7.160

ἐπανατίθημι.definition: lay upon, Ar.V.148; Med., shift one's position, of patients under operation, Gal.18.425

ἐπανατολή.definition: invisible rising of stars just after sunrise or sunset, Ptol.Alm.8.4

ἐπαναφορά.definition: referring, reference; reference of a question to an assembly, And.3.33; to the people, Harp

ἐπάνθημα.definition: efflorescence, fine flower, Id.in Nic.p.39 P., al.; special virtues, ib.p.118 P

ἐπανίστημι.definition: set up again, ib.778d; make to rise against, Plu.Sert.13; raise in revolt against, App.Hisp.101

ἐπανύω.definition: fut. complete, accomplish, Hes.Sc.311:—Med., procure, . . codd. in S.Tr.995 ; carry into effect, Ph.1.77

ἐπαξιόω.definition: think right, deem it right, c. inf; expect, believe, c. acc. et inf., . . . . ib.658; but . . deems thee worthy of honour, so as to render thee a due return, Id.OC1497

ἐπαπειλέω.definition: hold out as a threat to one; c. dat. only, threaten, Il.13.582

ἐπαπορέω.definition: raise a new doubt or question; c. dat., criticize, Diog.Oen.18

ἐπαραρίσκω.definition: aor. 1 aor. 2 to or; intr. in Ion. pf. plpf. tight or exactly, a cross-bolt was fitted therein, Il.12.456; part. close-fitting, well fixed, firm on his feet, Arat.83: also Ep. aor. part. Pass., well-fitted, prepared, …

ἐπαρήγω.definition: come to aid, help, Il.23.783, Od.13.391, E.El.1350 , Ar.V.402: abs., A.Ch.725 ; S.El.1197; also in Prose, X.Cyr.6.4.18, LXX2 Ma.13.17

ἐπαρκέω.definition: fut. : Ep. aor. inf; c. acc. rei, ward off, prevent, A.R.2.1161; S.Aj.360

ἐπαρτάω.definition: hang on or over; the elevated part of the beam, Arist.Mech.850a23

ἐπαρτύω.definition: and fit or fix on; prepare, Od.3.152; Opp.C.2.443:—Med., they prepared them a meal, h.Cer.128

ἐπαρυστήρ.definition: vessel for pouring oil into a lamp, LXXEx.25.37

ἐπαρύτω.definition: draw a liquid from one vessel into another, metaph. in Med., Plu.2.600d:—Act., dub. in D.Chr.12.70

ἐπαρχία.definition: the government of an or the; military 'command', force occupying a district, Ph.Bel.96.49

ἐπάρχω.definition: rule over, X.Cyr.4.6.2; rule besides one's hereditary dominions, X.Cyr.1.1.4

ἐπασκέω.definition: labour or toil at, prepare or finish; adorn, exalt, Pi.N.9.10, cf. Fr.194.4; Id.Parth.2.71

ἐπαύλημα.definition: musical phrase played on the flute, EM757.32

ἐπαυρέω.definition: Act., partake of, share, c.gen. rei, . . Il.18.302; . . Od.17.81; enjoys a greater share of night, of Sirius, Hes.Op.419; many have had enjoyment of neighbours, Pi.P.3.36; have enjoyment in the highest degree, Thgn.11…

ἐπαύω.definition: shout over, A.Ch.828 codd. ; in Theoc.23.44 is dub

ἐπαχλύω.definition: trans., darken, Them.Or.11.144c:—Pass., ib.19.232d. even in pres., A.R. l.c.; in Arat.906 Schneider restored for

ἐπεγείρω.definition: awaken, rouse up, Od.22.431, Thgn.469; erect, raise, erecting his prickles, like certain fish when irritated, Com.Adesp.1338 ; Philum.Ven.17.5

ἐπεγκλίνω.definition: incline, turn towards either side, v.l. in Gal.UP12.9

ἐπεγχύτης.definition: cup-bearer, so called by the Hellespontines, Demetr.Sceps. ap. Ath.10.425c

ἐπείγω.definition: Il.12.452, etc., Aeol. Hdn.Gr.2.436; drive on, urge forward, . . Od.12.205; freq. of a fair wind, 12.167; Il.15.382; S.Ph.1451

ἔπειμι.definition: to be upon, be set upon, of names, Hdt.6.53; so Pi.N.7.23; Ar.Nu.1025; to be attached, Anacreont.58.3; Pl.R.561d; esp. of rewards and penalties, A.Eu.543 , Ar.Av.597; S.El.1467; Is.3.47, cf. Pl.Lg.943d: abs., no count…

ἐπεκβάλλω.definition: prolong an incision, Antyll. ap; Geom., produce, Archim.Spir.Praef. ; Iamb.in Nic.p.57 P

ἐπέκπλοος.definition: contr. sailing out against, attack by sea, Id.8.20

ἐπελαύνω.definition: drive upon, i.e. upon; drive to a place, SIG1025.11

ἐπελεύθω.definition: aor. 1 bring a child to its father, Leg.Gort.3.45,al

ἐπέλπομαι.definition: Ep. poet. Verb, have hopes of, hope, c. inf. fut., . . Il.1.545; Od.21.126; . . A.Ag.1031 : generally, expect, Telest.1.1

ἐπεμβαίνω.definition: step or tread upon, in pf., stand upon, c; embark on ship-board, D.50.25

ἐπεμβολή.definition: insertion, parenthesis; placing over so as to fasten, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.33.4

ἐπεμπίπτω.definition: fall upon, attack furiously; fall to, set to work, Ar.Pax471

ἐπέξειμι.definition: serving as Att. fut. to; get out, escape, Arist.Pr.937a28

ἐπεξετάζω.definition: pass in review, feast one's eyes upon, Men.Pk.414

ἐπεξόδιος.definition: of a march or expedition: , sacrifices before the march of an army, v.l. in X.An.6.5.2

ἐπερείδω.definition: bring the whole force of the phalanx against, Plu.Flam.8: abs., Id.Pyrrh.21, cf. Arr.Tact.16.13:—Med., Ael.Tact.14.5

ἐπερέφω.definition: put a cover upon, roof, Il.1.39

ἐπερύω.definition: Ep. and Ion. pull to, Od.1.441; having dragged a stone to the top [of the tumulus], 12.14; draw to one, A.R.3.149:—Med., draw on one's clothes, Hdt.4.8

ἐπέρχομαι.definition: impf. Th.4.120 (unless fr; of persons, approach, c. dat., Il.12.200,218, etc.; esp. come suddenly upon, Od.19.155, Hdt.6.95: c. acc., E.HF593 codd. ; come to for advice, Id.Supp.155, Hel.165, cf. Pl.Lg.772d: with Prep…

ἐπέσθω.definition: Dor. and poet. for foreg., Epich.42.6, Call.Epigr.48

ἐπευφημέω.definition: assent with a shout of applause, c. inf; c. acc. pers., glorify, sing praises to her, Musae.275

ἐπεύχομαι.definition: pray or make a vow to a deity, c. dat; vow, c. fut. inf., A.Th.276

ἐπέχω.definition: hold out to, present, offer, Il.9.489; Od.16.444; . . Il.22.494; . . ib.83, cf. E.Andr.225; also I offered not mother's food with my breast, Id.Ion1492: c. inf., Ar.Nu.1382: abs., Id.Pax1167:—Med., having put it to hi…

ἐπηλυσία.definition: Ep. coming over one, esp. by; approach, Nonn.D.14.328

ἐπηπύω.definition: shout in applause, Il.18.502: abs., shout, Orph.A.528

ἐπηρέμησις.definition: pause between systole and diastole of pulse, ib.184,al

ἐπιάλλω.definition: fut. aor. upon, laid hands upon them, Od.9.288; 15.475; for this man brought these deeds to pass, 22.49; also in Com., I will lay it on, Ar.Nu.1299, cf. Fr.552 , Phryn.Com.1

ἐπιαύω.definition: sleep among, c. dat., v.l; sleep upon, AP6.192

ἐπιάχω.definition: shout out, shout applause after a speech

ἐπιβαίνω.definition: rarely imper. Thgn.847, Dor; get upon, mount on, Il.8.165; ib.512; 5.328, 10.513; 23.379; 9.133; Hdt.9.70; A.Supp.39; also Hdt.8.118: freq. in Hom., in aor. Med., Od.6.78, al

ἐπιβάλλω.definition: add, contribute, Arist.Metaph.993b2; Thphr.Ign.49; Pl.Cra.409b: metaph., throw in, mention, dub. in S.El.1246 ; . . Sch.Pi.P.4.28: abs., bid higher, Arist.Pol.1259a14

ἐπιβαρέω.definition: weigh down: hence, be a burden to, 1; Pass., of a bandage, to be found irksome, PMed.Lond.3.39

ἐπιβάσκω.definition: causal of c. gen., lead them into misery, Il.2.234

ἐπιβήτης.definition: one who sets foot on or dwells in, Orph.Fr.353

ἐπιβλής.definition: bolt or bar fitting into a socket; cover, ib.7.479

ἐπιβομβέω.definition: make a booming noise with; ring, Nonn.D.40.503

ἐπιβρέμω.definition: roar out, E.Ba.151: abs., ring, Musae.193; Q.S.14.458

ἐπιβρέχω.definition: pour water on, water, cj. for in; impers., it rains, Simp.in Epict.p.92D

ἐπιβρίθω.definition: fall heavy upon, fall heavily, of rain; trans., press on, J.BJ3.7.23; press home, Opp.H.2.467

ἐπιβρύω.definition: fut. burst over, as water: of flowers, burst forth, Theoc.22.43; to be overrun by . . , Alciphr.1.17

ἐπιγίγνομαι.definition: Ion. and later fut; of Time, to be born after, come into being after, 11.6.148; of persons, Hdt.7.2; posterity, Id.9.85; who came after him, Id.2.49; the new must prevail over the old, Th.1.71, cf. Pl.R.574a; . . X.Cy…

ἐπιγιγνώσκω.definition: Ion. and later look upon; of things, find out, discover, A.Ag.1598, cf. Th.1.132, etc.; Plb.2.11.3; . . would you recognize when it became your own?, Pl.Euthd.301e; IG9.313 ; . . Arist.HA631b11; Plb.1.65.6, cf. POxy.9…

ἐπιγνάμπτω.definition: metaph., bow, bend to one's purpose, Il.2.14; 1.569; 9.514:—Med., Nic.Al.363

ἐπιγράφω.definition: mark the surface, graze; write upon, inscribe, Hdt.3.88; Id.4.88; Th.1.132, cf. D.59.97; . . Id.18.289: abs., IG12.76.43; esp. write or place an epitaph on a tomb, ib.14.1835, al., 7.2543.9: Med., have inscribed, Ar.A…

ἐπιδέκατος.definition: containing an integer and one-tenth; one in ten: hence Subst

ἐπιδεύομαι.definition: Ep. for II), to be; to be lacking in, fall short of, c. gen. rei, 23.670, cf. 17.142: also c. gen. pers., fallest far short of them, 5.636; or both together, 24.385: later c. acc. rei, A.R.2.1220.—The Act. occurs only…

ἐπιδέω.definition: fut. bind, fasten on; bind up, bandage, Hp.VC13, Fract.21, Art.14:—Pass., with one's wounds bound up, X.Cyr.5.2.32, al.; ib.2.3.19

ἐπιδημεύω.definition: = sq., live among the people, live in the throng, opp. live in the country, Od.16.28

ἐπιδημέω.definition: to be at home, live at home, opp; of diseases, to be prevalent, epidemic, Hp.Prog.25

ἐπιδιαρρέω.definition: flow through or melt away besides, Erot. s.v

ἐπιδίδωμι.definition: give besides, Il.23.559; of a physician, administer, Ph.1.253; give afterwards, Dsc.4.148

ἐπίδικος.definition: disputed at law, liable to be made the; Subst. an heiress for whose hand her next of kin are claimants at law, Is.3.64; ib.73

ἐπιδινέω.definition: whirl for the throw, swing round before throwing, Il.3.378, cf. Od.9.538, etc.:—Med., turn over in one's mind, resolve, 20.218:—Pass., wheel about, as birds in the air, 2.151; . . Nic.Al.33; so of drones, Arist.HA624a24

ἐπιδοιάζω.definition: entertain doubts over, turn over and over, A.R.3.21; cf

ἐπιδοξάζω.definition: form an opinion about a thing:—Pass., matter of opinion, Thphr.CP1.5.5

ἐπιδοτήρ.definition: giver of more, opp. of planets, Ptol.Tetr.189

ἐπιδράω.definition: perform over a person, of purificatory rites, Philostr.VA6.5

ἐπίδρομος.definition: that may be overrun, a wall; metaph., intelligible, Them.Or.13.162c

ἐπιεικής.definition: fitting, meet, suitable; of statements, rights, etc

ἐπιέννυμι.definition: put on besides or over, we threw a cloak over him, Od.20.143: elsewh. Hom. has only pf. part. Pass. : in metaph. sense c. acc., clad in shamelessness, strength, Il.1.149, 8.262, etc.; AP7.283 ; covered with hair over …

ἐπίζευξις.definition: fastening together, joining; Gramm., repetition of a word, Hdn.Fig.p.99 S., Phoeb.Fig.1.3

ἐπιζυγίς.definition: iron pin upon which the strands of; cross beam, Apollod.Poliorc.172.7

ἐπιθαρσύνω.definition: Att. cheer on, encour Il.4.183, D.H.10.41, Plu.Mar.36

ἐπιθέω.definition: run upon, at or after, Hdt.9.107, X.Cyn.6.10; metaph., Plot.2.9.6; to be diffused over, Id.5.3.17, al

ἐπιθεωρέω.definition: examine over again or carefully, ascertain; consider next in order, Epicur.Nat.13G

ἐπιθεωρία.definition: Astrol., aspecting from the right, Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.155.15

ἐπιθήγω.definition: whetor sharpen yet more, Ael.NA5.16: metaph., stimulate yet more, Plu.786b

ἐπιθρῴσκω.definition: leap upon, c. gen; leap over a space, so far do [the horses] spring at a bound, 5.772; Hes.Sc.438

ἐπιθύω.definition: sacrifice upon, h.Ap.491; burn incense, LXX3 Ki.12.33, J.BJ7.3.3, D.S.12.11, 18.61, Porph.Abst.2.59; D.S.18.61, v.l. in Ar.Pl.1116: generally, offer on, D.H.1.40 codd

ἐπίκαιρος.definition: in fit time or place, seasonable; serious, important, important symptoms, Hp.Epid.1.25; Id.Acut

ἐπίκαυμα.definition: blister caused by a burn, A; ulcer on the eye, esp. the cornea, Gal.12.758, 14.774, 19.434

ἐπίκειμαι.definition: serving as Pass. to to be laid; of doors, to be put to or closed , Od.6.19: metaph., Thgn.421

ἐπικείρω.definition: Ep. aor. 1 cut off, cut down; metaph., cut short, baffle, Il.15.467, cf. 16.120

ἐπικέλλω.definition: aor. 1 also Act.Ap.27.41; abs., run ashore, Od.9.138; A.R.3.575: c.acc., Id.2.352; also of the ship itself, Od.13.114; of a fish, rush into the net, Numen. ap. Ath.7.321b

ἐπικεράννυμι.definition: mix in addition, mix fresh wine, Od.7.164, cf. Gal.18.169:—Med., Damocr. ap. eund.14.100

ἐπικερτομέω.definition: mock, used by Hom. only in part; c. acc., he reproached him, Hdt.8.92; for a thing, Agath.5.22; tease, banter, Theoc.20.2, cf. Luc.Bis Acc.12

ἐπικεύθω.definition: conceal, hide, always with a neg., Il.5.816; Od.5.143; . . 15.263; 4.744, cf. 17.141: and in A.Ag.800 , c. acc., I will not hide it from thee, cf. A.R.3.332

ἐπικηρόω.definition: wax over, rub with wax, Polyaen.2.20

ἐπικίδνημι.definition: spread over, spread a brave spirit over your ills, Orac. ap. Hdt.7.140:-in Hom. always Pass. , is spread over the earth, Il.2.850, cf. A.R.2.978; far as the morning light is spread, Il.7.451,458; Q.S.5.347

ἐπικληρόω.definition: Dor. assign by lot; have assigned one by lot, D.C.37.50

ἐπικλίνω.definition: put to, shut a door: hence, in Pass., once; bend towards, prick the ears, X.Cyn.6.15; lean against . . , Paus.9.30.10; Philostr.Her.19.11; pull it open, Arist.PA660b22:—Pass., spars leaning on the wall and inclined at…

ἐπικλύω.definition: listen to, hear, c. acc., Il.23.652, cf. A.R.3.598; S.Ichn.39: c.gen., Od.5.150, cf. A.R.1.1240, Eratosth.19

ἐπικλώθω.definition: spin upon, Hermipp.48; elsewh; spin to one, assign, prop. of the Fates who spun the thread of destiny; also of all powers which influence men's fortunes, Od.3.208, cf.4.208, etc.; Callin.1.9, cf. Them.Or.32.356d:—Med.…

ἐπικνάω.definition: scrape or grate over; scratch, Hld.2.8

ἐπικοπή.definition: cutting close, pollarding, of trees; cutting down, felling, fall by a single blow, D.C.38.50, 49.29

ἐπικόπτω.definition: pf. Phld.D.1.15:—strike upon (i.e; later, of trees, lop, pollard, Thphr.CP5.17.3; cut down brushwood, PLond.3.1170B26 : metaph., cut short, bring down from high estate, Arist.Pol.1284b2; Plu.2.529b; check, impede, ib.…

ἐπικουρέω.definition: to be an act as an ally, once in; serve as allies or mercenaries, Isoc.4.168; Pl.R.575b

ἐπικραίνω.definition: Ep. 3sg. fut. dub. in A.Ag.1340 codd.: aor. 1 Ep. :—Med., 3pl. aor. 1 Q.S.14.297:—bring to pass, accomplish, may he fulfil it, Il.15.599; he fulfilled it not for them,3.302, cf. 2.419 ; grant me this prayer, fulfil it…

ἐπίκρανον.definition: that which is put on the head, head-

ἐπικρατέω.definition: prevail in battle, be victorious, [to them] though they are victorious as it is, Il.14.98, cf. Ar.Lys.767; conquer or die, Hdt.7.104; Id.1.173; gain the advantage in most points in the war, Th.4.19

ἐπικυέω.definition: simply, become pregnant again, BGU1058.30 , al

ἐπιλάμπω.definition: shine after or thereupon; shine upon , abs., Hp.Aër.6, X.Cyn.8.1: c.dat., Plu.Fab.6; Id.Arat.22, cf. Theo Sm.p.121H.: metaph., . . AP5.16 ; bring them new light; OGI194.20 , cf. ib.669.7

ἐπιλείβω.definition: also pour wine over a thing, Il.1.462; A.R.1.1133: abs., Od.3.341

ἐπιλεύσσω.definition: look towards or at, one can only see so far before one, Il.3.12

ἐπιλήθω.definition: cause to forget; Med., or more commonly Aeol. and Dor. Alc.Supp.25.6, S.El.146 , fut. aor. 2 Pl.Ap.17a: late aor. 1 Nonn.D.48.969: with pf. Act. Hdt.3.46, Pi.O. , but more freq. E.Ba.188, Ar.Nu.631, Lys.26.1, Pl.Phd.7…

ἐπιληκέω.definition: clap the hands in applause, or beat time to the dancers, Od.8.379

ἐπίληψις.definition: taking hold of, clasping; in Law, claiming property by seizing, Pl.Lg.954e

ἐπιλλίζω.definition: make signs to one by winking; blink, when drowsy, Nic.Th.163

ἐπιλύζω.definition: Ep. have the hiccough besides, Nic.Al.81

ἐπιλωβεύω.definition: make mockery of a thing, Od.2.323

ἐπιμαίομαι.definition: c. acc., lay hold of, grasp, he clutched his sword-hilt, Od.11.531; . . ib.591; having clutched [the sword] with my hand, 9.302, cf. 19.480; took her by the hand, A.R.3.106

ἐπιμαχέω.definition: stand by, help one in battle, for the mutual defence of their countries, Th.5.27

ἐπίμαχος.definition: that may easily be attacked; contended for, contested, Hld.8.1

ἐπιμειδάω.definition: smile at or upon, in Hom. always in phrase, he addressed him with a smile, Il.4.356, al.; in 10.400, of a scornful smile; but Hes.Th.547: c.dat., AP6.345

ἐπιμέμφομαι.definition: cast blame upon, c.dat. pers; c. acc. rei, impute as matter of blame, Hdt.1.75, cf. 2.161, etc

ἐπιμένω.definition: stay on, tarry, abs., Il.19.142, Od.17.277; 11.351; do you wait, and I will put on my armour, Il.6.340; also . . . . Od.4.587; . . h.Cer.160, Ar.Nu.196; so . . X.An.5.5.2: after Hom., remain in a place, And.1.75, etc.…

ἐπιμερής.definition: superpartient, of numbers of the form 1+2/x, 1+3/x, etc., Theo Sm.p.76H., Nicom.Ar.1.17, al.; cf

ἐπιμήδομαι.definition: imagine or contrive a thing against one, Od.4.437, cf. Q.S.14.479

ἐπιμηνάω.definition: 3pl. pf. = they have been content to wait, Schwyzer91.11

ἐπιμηνίω.definition: to be angry with, Il.13.460, cf. App.BC3.55; Id.Mith.55

ἐπιμιμνήσκομαι.definition: fut. Hdt.1.5, etc., rarely; make mention of, ib.191, cf. Hdt.1.5,85, A.Ch.l.c., S.Ph.1400, etc.; `but, by the way', Herod.5.53, cf. 6.42; also Hdt.2.101, X.Cyr.1.6.12, Pl.Mx.239c, etc.: with neut. pron. in acc., Hdt.1…

ἐπιμίμνω.definition: poet. for abide or continue in, Od.14.66, 15.372

ἐπιμίσγω.definition: older poet. and Ion. form (found also in; mostly Pass., in Il. always in hostile sense, I have always to be dealing with the Trojans, am always clashing with them, Il.10.548; as the fight was joined again, 5.505; in O…

ἐπιμύζω.definition: murmur or mutter at another's words, Il.4.20 :—Med., Hsch

ἐπιμύω.definition: pf. Sor.2.27:—close the eyes; wink at, in token of assent, Ar.V.934

ἐπινάω.definition: send forth emanations or influences, Ascl.in Metaph.23.5:—Pass., ib.120.2, cf. 186.1

ἐπινέμω.definition: allot, distribute; turn one's cattle to graze on another's land, Id.Lg.843d; Arist.Pol.1305a26, cf.D.55.11; enjoy right of pasturage, Berl.Sitzb.1927.7

ἐπινεύω.definition: make a sign to another to do a thing, order him to do, c. inf., . . Il.9.620:abs., Od.16.164 , h.Cer.169,466, X.Cyr.5.5.37

ἐπινέω.definition: spin to, esp. like of the Fates, span for him with her thread at his birth, Il.20.128,24.210: —Pass., Ael.NA7.1, cf. Fr.260; Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.14

ἐπινηνέω.definition: Ep.for , only in impf., heap or pile upon, c. gen. loci, Il.7.428; perh. to be read in Iamb.VP3.17

ἐπινόημα.definition: thought, purpose, contrivance; conception, Epicur.Nat.130,137 G

ἐπινόμιον.definition: payment for pasturage, IG5.456; = sq.1, title of work ascribed to Plato, Theo Sm.pp.7,84,178H

ἐπινομίς.definition: addition to a law, appendix, name; new-year's gift, Ath.3.97d

ἐπινοτίζω.definition: sprinkle on the surface, Dsc.2.83.2; Pass., perspire slightly, Philum. ap. Aët.5.78

ἐπιξέω.definition: scrape or graze on the surface, Hp.VC14 , Aret.CD1.2; Hld.5.14: metaph., polish a poem, Vit.Apollon.Rhod

ἐπίξυνος.definition: poet. for a common field, in which several persons have rights, Il.12.422

ἐπιορκέω.definition: also IG22.1126.9; simply, = swear, Sol. ap. Lys.10.17

ἐπιόσσομαι.definition: have before one's eyes, Il.17.381; gaze on, A.R.2.28 ; i.e.live, Nic.Th.276

ἐπιπείθομαι.definition: to be persuaded; trust to, put faith in, A.Ag.1095 , cf. IG14.1389ii 32

ἐπιπέλομαι.definition: come to or upon, . . Od.15.408, cf. 13.60: elsewh. only in Ep. aor.2 part. rolling on, approaching, when the eighth revolving year had come, 7.261; Hes.Sc.87, Th.493 ; A.R.2.1231, 4.670, etc.; of persons, Id.3.25,127;…

ἐπιπέτομαι.definition: fut. Hdt.7.15: aor. or; c.acc., fly over, E.Hel.1486 ; Ar.Av.118; Ael.NA17.16: metaph., fly over to, run eagerly after, Ar.Av.1471 ; flitting from one to another, Pl.R.365a

ἐπιπίλναμαι.definition: only pres., Ep. for come near, Od.6.44 ; Il.19.92

ἐπιπίπτω.definition: fall upon or over; of money, accrue, SIG953.66

ἐπιπλάζομαι.definition: fut. aor. I about over, Od.8.14; A.R.3.1066:—later in Act., Nic.Al.127

ἐπιπλέω.definition: sail against, attack by sea, Hdt.5.86; Th.3.76; X.HG1.5.11, etc.; D.S.20.50: abs., Hdt.1.70, 6.33; also of the ships, Th.3.80: generally, sail on, Plb.1.25.4, etc

ἐπιπλήσσω.definition: punish, chastise, esp. with words, rebuke. reprove, c.acc.pers., Il.23.580, cf. Pl.Prt.327a: c. dat., Il.12.211, cf. Isoc.1.31; Pl.Lg.805b, cf. 1 Ep.Ti.5.1, etc.; for a thing, Pl.Plt.286b:—Pass., to be rebuked, Id.Grg…

ἐπιπνέω.definition: Ep. (as always in Hom., cf; blow furiously upon, Hdt.3.26: metaph., . . A.Th.343 , cf. S.Ant.136

ἐπιπρέπω.definition: to be conspicuous; beseem, suit, c. dat., Plu.2.794a: impers., it is fitting, c.inf., Xenoph.26

ἐπιπταίρω.definition: sneeze at, he sneezed as I spoke the words , Od.17.545, cf. h.Merc.297, Nonn.D.7.107: metaph., to be gracious to, favour, Theoc.7.96; Id.18.16

ἐπίπτυξις.definition: application to one another of vocal cords, Gal.UP7.13

ἐπιπωλέομαι.definition: go about, go through, c.acc., of the general inspecting his troops, Il.3.196, etc.; but in 11.264, of reconnoitring an enemy.—Them. has visit, Or.6.75c: c. dat., ib.11.152b

ἐπιπώρωμα.definition: callus formed over the fracture; gouty concretion, Id.Prorrh.2.8

ἐπιρράσσω.definition: Ep. dash to, shut violently; dash against, throw the cavalry upon them, Id.3.25; Nonn.D.11.195; strike, ib.41.189

ἐπιρρέζω.definition: offer sacrifices at a place; sacrifice afterwards or besides, Theoc.24.99, cf.AP6.157 ; GDI3639a5 : abs., IG12.677.29

ἐπιρρέπω.definition: metaph., incline, Ph.2.582; trans., force down one scale, Thgn.157

ἐπιρρέω.definition: late fut. HeroSpir.1.9: aor. 1 Act; flow in besides, keep on flowing, . . . . Heraclit.12; , Ar.Nu.1294; Pl.Ti.85e; ib.22e: metaph. of large bodies of men, stream on, Il.11.724; Hdt.9.38; Pl.Phdr.229d; of a flood of t…

ἐπιρρίπτω.definition: apply a plaster or fomentation, Sor.1.50 , 69; Dsc.5.88; Pass., spreading over the surface, Id.1.42

ἐπιρροθέω.definition: shout in answer or in approval; c. acc., rage against, abuse him, S.Tr.264

ἐπίρροθος.definition: coming to the rescue; as Subst; reproaches bandied backwards and forwards, abusive language, S.Ant.413

ἐπιρρώομαι.definition: old Ep. pres.: aor.1 Med; move nimbly, Hes.Th.8, cf. A.R.1.385 : c. acc. cogn., urge the rapid dance, AP9.403

ἐπισαλπίζω.definition: accompany on the trumpet; blow the horns, ib.7.14.5

ἐπισάττω.definition: pile a load upon; heap up, Thphr.HP7.2.5

ἐπισείω.definition: Ep. , shake at or; urge on, S.Fr.147; set them upon one, E.Or.255; ib.613; Alex.3; hurl at, Parth.14.4

ἐπισεύω.definition: mostly Pass., hurry or hasten to or towards, Il.2.86; 13.757; to pasture, 18.575; Od.13.19; in hostile sense, rush upon or at, c. dat., Il.15 347

ἐπίσημον.definition: distinguishing mark, device, badge; generally, mark, imprint, S.Ichn.102

ἐπισίτιος.definition: working for his victuals alone; provision-money, Lys.Fr.75 S

ἐπίσκηνος.definition: at or before the tent, i.e. public; the soldiers quartered , Plu.Sert.24, cf. sq

ἐπίσκοπος.definition: one who watches over; scout, watch, c.dat., one set to watch them, Il.10.38,342

ἐπισκύζομαι.definition: to be indignant at a thing, Il.9.370; Od.7.306: —Act., aor. EM364.10

ἐπισκύλλω.definition: in Pass., aor. 2 part. after being temporarily distressed, Vett.Val.171.18

ἐπισπάω.definition: draw or drag after one; metaph., bring on, cause, A.Pers.477

ἐπισπένδω.definition: pour upon or over, esp. as a drink-; promise, pledge, Leg.Gort.4.52, 6.11:—Med., accept in pledge, ib.6.13, al

ἐπισπέρχω.definition: follow close upon the track, Opp.C.4.96: abs., Nic.Th.144; intr., rage furiously, Od.5.304, cf. Pi.Parth.2.18; Aret.CA1.8

ἐπίσταμαι.definition: know how to do, be able to do, capable of doing, c.inf., Il.21.320, cf. Od.13.207, Sapph.70, etc.: Hom. has it both of intellectual power, Il.14.92; Od.4.730; and of artistic skill, Il.5.60: freq. in Trag. and Att., A…

ἐπισταχύω.definition: shoot or sprout forth, prop. of corn: metaph. of the beard, A.R.1.972

ἐπιστέφω.definition: in Hom. always in Med; to be full of or covered with, Alcm.74 B

ἐπιστρέφω.definition: pf. Diog. :—turn; intr., turn about, turn round, Il.3.370; here only in Hom., and perh. trans., whirl, but v. Hdt.2.103, S.Tr.566; Ar.V.422; of ships, put about, Plb.1.47.8, 50.5; of a wild boar, turn upon the hunter,…

ἐπιστρωφάω.definition: Frequentat. of only intr., c. acc., visit or frequent a place, .. Od.17.486; haunt him, h.Merc.44; Orph.A.830; Phryn.Trag.5:—Med., go in and out of, frequent, haunt, A.Ag.972; also, come to, E.Med.666

ἐπιστύφω.definition: draw up, of the effect of astringents; apply a second mordant, as preparation for dyeing, PHolm.16.28

ἐπισυνάγω.definition: collect and bring to a place; bring in, in a discussion, Phld.Acad.Ind.28

ἐπισυναφή.definition: in Music, combination of three; Rhet., subjoining, Anon.Fig.p.146S

ἐπισύρω.definition: drag or trail after one; draw gently, Alciphr.3.12

ἐπισφαλής.definition: prone to fall, unstable; making to fall, misleading, Plu.2.653d, etc

ἐπίσχω.definition: redupl. pres. of hold or direct towards; restrain, keep in check, Hes.Sc.446; Th.3.45, cf. Pl.Lg.932e, Phlb.45d; obstruction, Arist.Cael.311a9: c. gen., Od.20.266; Pl.Hp.Ma.298a:—Med., girding up, h.Cer.176; Euphro8.3…

ἐπιτελής.definition: brought to an end, completed; Act., effective, Ant.Lib.19.3

ἐπιτέλλω.definition: aor. aor. A.R.3.264:—Pass., 3sg. plpf. .. Il.2.643:—enjoin, prescribe, command, Hom., etc.—Constr.: c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, spake a speech of command to her, Od.23.349 : c. acc. rei only, Il.1.25, etc.; .. 11.840; …

ἐπιτέμνω.definition: Ion. fut. Antyll. (v; make a further incision, opp. Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.2

ἐπιτέρπομαι.definition: Ep. Verb , rejoice or delight in, Od.14.228, cf. Hes.Th.158; Pi.O.5.22; Thgn.1218; h.Ap.204; ib.146 : c. inf., AP9.766

ἐπίτευξις.definition: hitting the mark, attainment; success, App.Pun.105

ἐπίτηκτος.definition: overlaid with gold; with gold or gilded ornaments laid on, IG22.1386.16; ib.1544.13

ἐπιτήκω.definition: melt upon, pour when melted over a thing, Hdt.7.239; Plu.Ages.40

ἐπιτίθημι.definition: Pass. mostly furnished by; set upon, turn towards, Il.10.46; but c. inf., put it into her mind to.., Od.21.1

ἐπιτίμιον.definition: mostly in pl., value; the honours paid to a person, S.El.915
